title: Journal and storage
scope:
This category covers how the C++ MDS makes metadata durable and where it stores it: the per-rank MDLog/Journaler (objects, header, framing, envelope, write path, flush triggers, ordered completion, segments, expiry, trimming, replay, recovery, the journal side of standby-replay and fencing before replay), the journal event types and their replay semantics, the RADOS object catalog of the metadata and data pools (naming, special inode numbers, dirfrag omap objects with embedded inodes, base inodes, mdsdir and strays, backtraces and other object-0 xattrs, data-object truncation, size probes and uninlining), the MDS tables (MDSTable, InoTable and inode-number allocation, SessionMap, the table server/client 2PC with the SnapTable object, the OpenFileTable) and the MDS as a RADOS client (Objecter, identity, full flags, OSDMap following, the OSD epoch barrier, write-error policy, pool requirements). Client eviction with blocklisting and blocklist-driven session kills are catalogued in 02-client-sessions-and-protocol; the MDS_TRIM, MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO and replay-time health checks in 11-security-admin-and-observability.

Sources are the fact-checked map pages [mdlog-and-journaler](../cpp-map/06-journal/mdlog-and-journaler.md), [events-and-replay](../cpp-map/06-journal/events-and-replay.md), [rados-object-catalog](../cpp-map/07-storage-formats/rados-object-catalog.md), [mds-tables](../cpp-map/07-storage-formats/mds-tables.md) and [rados-and-osd-interactions](../cpp-map/07-storage-formats/rados-and-osd-interactions.md). Because the new MDS never reads C++ MDS data, on-disk formats here are free unless another component reads or writes the object; each entry's relied_on_by therefore names the peers that touch it (clients for data-object naming, inode numbers, truncate_seq and inline_version; cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-table-tool, first-damage.py and ceph-dencoder for metadata objects; mgr modules for objects that share the metadata pool).

Excluded and owned elsewhere: the PurgeQueue journal, stray purging, scrub, the damage table and repair (09-background-services); snapshot ids, MRemoveSnaps, snapdiff/blockdiff and rstat semantics (08); dirfrag split/merge policy and directory size limits (05); max_size, file-recovery triggers and inode delegation for async create (03); session eviction policy, reclaim and laggy-OSD eviction deferral (02); layouts and their vxattrs (04); Mantle (07); rank states, failover, standby-replay state handling and resolve/rejoin (01). Where an entry touches those mechanisms it describes only the storage or journal part and links to the owning map page.

Cross-category review (2026-10-11): entries that duplicated an entry of the owning category were retired (listed under "retired" in features.json with the entry they were merged into) or shortened to pointers whose description starts with "See F-XXX-NNN." and keeps only the facts specific to this category.

groups.name: Journal on-disk format
groups.intro: The per-rank journal as RADOS objects: pointer, header, striped byte stream, entry framing and the event envelope. The format is private to the MDS except for cephfs-journal-tool and ceph-dencoder, which parse it exactly.

groups.name: Journal write path and durability
groups.intro: How an event becomes durable: submission order, group commit, flush triggers (including the client FLUSH_MDLOG request), ordered completion, the safe reply, and journal I/O error handling.

groups.name: Segments, expiry and trimming
groups.intro: LogSegments as units of lazy writeback, segment boundaries, background and explicit trimming, and capping the log when a rank stops.

groups.name: Journal event types
groups.intro: The event payloads: EMetaBlob after-images and the event types that carry namespace, session, open-file, 2PC, migration and fragmentation records. Table events are in the table groups.

groups.name: Journal recovery and replay
groups.intro: Opening the journal, finding its end, replaying it into the cache and tables, error policy, single-writer fencing and the journal side of standby-replay.

groups.name: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
groups.intro: The backing store of the namespace in the metadata pool: object naming, special inode numbers, dirfrag omap objects with embedded inodes, base inodes, the per-rank mdsdir and strays, mkfs and boot-time loading. These objects are private to the MDS but parsed by offline repair tools.

groups.name: Backtraces and data-pool objects
groups.intro: What the MDS stores on or does to objects in data pools: backtrace and layout xattrs (read by open_ino and cephfs-data-scan), the client-shared data-object naming, truncation, size recovery and uninlining.

groups.name: InoTable and SessionMap
groups.intro: Per-rank inode number allocation (InoTable, session preallocation, release, no reuse) and the per-rank SessionMap object.

groups.name: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
groups.intro: The cluster-global table mechanism (only instance: the snap table on rank 0): its object, the MDS-to-MDS two-phase commit, journaling, recovery and resolve hooks. What snapshots mean is owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes.

groups.name: OpenFileTable
groups.intro: The per-rank OpenFileTable: a non-authoritative persistent record of open inodes and their ancestors that lets journal segments expire without re-journaling opens and lets a recovering rank prefetch inodes.

groups.name: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
groups.intro: The MDS as a RADOS client: its Objecter, identity, full-flag handling, OSDMap following, completion path, client blocklisting and the OSD epoch barrier, write-error policy and pool requirements.

groups.name: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
groups.intro: Health warnings, perf counters and status output tied to the journal and tables; offline tools that read or write the C++ formats; developer and fault-injection options.

features.name: Journal pointer object (front/back journal inode)
features.summary: Per-rank object that names the active journal inode, so whichever daemon holds the rank finds its journal.
features.description: Object `<0x400+rank>.00000000` in the metadata pool (default namespace) holds `JournalPointer` `ENCODE_START(1,1)`{u64 front, u64 back}. `front` is the active journal inode (`0x200+rank`, or `0x300+rank` after a format rewrite); `back` is non-zero only while a rewrite is in progress. The mds-log-recvr thread reads it with a blocking `read_full`: `-ENOENT` creates `{front=0x200+rank, back=0}`, `-EBLOCKLISTED` respawns, any other read or decode error marks the rank damaged. It is written with `write_full` (asynchronously at mkfs, blocking elsewhere).
features.notes: cephfs-journal-tool (JournalScanner, Dumper, Resetter) reads it; `journal reset --force` rewrites it to `{0x200+rank, 0}`. A failure to create the pointer after `-ENOENT` marks the rank damaged whatever the error, also for `-EBLOCKLISTED` (src/mds/MDLog.cc:1095-1104; rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 29). QA test_damage expects a deleted pointer object not to damage the rank (it is recreated).

legacy_parts.note: A non-zero back pointer and a front of 0x300+rank, which only the legacy-format journal rewrite produces, and the erase of a back journal left by an interrupted rewrite. _reformat_journal is the only user of the alternate inode 0x300+rank (MDS_INO_LOG_BACKUP_OFFSET), and it runs only for journals whose stream format is below mds_journal_format (format 0, written by C++ releases before v0.82 or with that dev option set to 0). mkfs (MDLog::create) and a pointer recreated after -ENOENT write {0x200+rank, 0}.

features.name: Journaler header object
features.summary: Object 0 of the journal records trimmed, expire and write positions, the layout and the stream format.
features.description: Object `<journal ino>.00000000` is always written whole (`write_full`) with `Journaler::Header` `ENCODE_START(2,2)`{string magic `"ceph fs volume v011"`, u64 trimmed_pos, u64 expire_pos, u64 unused_field (written as expire_pos), u64 write_pos, legacy 28-byte `ceph_file_layout`, u8 stream_format (0 LEGACY, 1 RESILIENT)}. `write_pos` is the Journaler safe position at header-write time, a lower bound of the real end; replay starts at `expire_pos`; objects below `trimmed_pos` may be gone. On read the header is rejected with `-EINVAL` if the magic differs or `write_pos < expire_pos` or `expire_pos < trimmed_pos`; a zero-length object is an empty journal; a missing object returns `-ENOENT`. The legacy layout encoding cannot carry a pool namespace, and a header whose layout pool differs from the metadata pool aborts the daemon.
features.notes: Same header format for the PurgeQueue journal (`0x500+rank`). cephfs-journal-tool `header get/set` edits trimmed_pos, expire_pos, write_pos and pool_id; `header set pool_id` is the documented repair for the pool-mismatch abort (src/tools/cephfs/JournalTool.cc:373). ceph-dencoder decodes `Journaler::Header`.

features.name: Striped journal byte stream and its RADOS objects
features.summary: The journal is an append-only byte stream striped over objects named after the journal inode.
features.description: A `file_layout_t` maps stream offsets to objects `"%llx.%08llx"` (journal ino, object index) in the metadata pool default namespace; rank 0 uses `200.00000000` (header), `200.00000001`, ... The layout is taken from `MDCache::gen_default_log_layout` (4 MiB objects, stripe_count 1, or `mds_log_segment_size` as object size and stripe unit when > 0) only when a journal is created; afterwards the header layout wins. Data starts at offset one period (object 1). RADOS ops: entries are `WRITE` at their offset through Filer (never `APPEND`), the header is `WRITEFULL`, prezeroing is `DELETE`/`ZERO`, the recovery probe is `STAT` with `RWORDERED`, replay reads use `FADVISE_DONTNEED`, trimming and erase are `DELETE`. Journal writes carry `FADVISE_DONTNEED` unless the MDSMap shows a standby-replay follower for the rank.
features.notes: The write IO hint is re-evaluated on every MDSMap received while up:active and is 0 (no hint) before that. Journal object names are rank-private: prezeroing deletes whatever exists at names ahead of the write position (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 26).

features.name: RESILIENT journal entry framing
features.summary: Per-entry framing with a sentinel and the entry start offset, so readers and tools can detect and skip damage.
features.description: In stream_format 1 every entry is: le64 sentinel `0x3141592653589793`, le32 payload length N, N payload bytes (one encoded LogEvent), le64 start_ptr = absolute stream offset of the entry (a 20-byte envelope). There is no checksum. A bad sentinel makes the reader fail with `-EINVAL`; `Journaler::try_read_entry` asserts `start_ptr == read_pos`. The sentinel and start_ptr exist so that offline tools can resynchronise in damaged journals: JournalScanner slides byte by byte to the next sentinel and checks start_ptr. LEGACY (format 0) framing is only `le32 length` + payload.
features.notes: PurgeQueue journals always use RESILIENT. Older-format MDLog journals are rewritten at open (F-STORE-006).

legacy_parts.note: LEGACY (stream_format 0) framing: le32 length plus payload without sentinel or start_ptr. Format 0 journals come from C++ releases before v0.82 (mds_journal_format, commit 68b200940c5) or from a C++ MDS whose dev option mds_journal_format is 0. MDLog::create uses that option (default 1, RESILIENT), and the PurgeQueue always creates RESILIENT journals.

features.name: LogEvent envelope and event type ids
features.summary: Versioned envelope that tags each journal payload with its event type.
features.description: Each payload is le32 `EVENT_NEW_ENCODING` (0) followed by `ENCODE_START(1,1)`{le32 event type, the event body with its own `ENCODE_START`}; decode also accepts the pre-versioned "classic" form whose first word is the type. Twenty type ids map to 18 classes: SUBTREEMAP 2, EXPORT 3, IMPORTSTART 4, IMPORTFINISH 5, FRAGMENT 6, RESETJOURNAL 9, SESSION 10, SESSIONS_OLD 11, SESSIONS 12, UPDATE 20, PEERUPDATE 21, OPEN 22, COMMITTED 23, PURGED 24, TABLECLIENT 42, TABLESERVER 43, SUBTREEMAP_TEST 50, NOOP 51, SEGMENT 100, LID 101. An unknown type or a decode exception returns nullptr (treated as a corrupt event), but bytes left after a successfully decoded event trip `ceph_assert(p.end())` and abort the daemon. Bodies are encoded with `MDLog::mdsmap_up_features`, a single member overwritten by every submission, so embedded entity_inst_t/address encodings follow the up-MDS feature set of the most recent submission rather than the event's own.
features.notes: The type names are the strings accepted by `cephfs-journal-tool --type` (src/mds/LogEvent.cc:77-129); `str_to_type` throws on an unknown name. ceph-dencoder decodes most events (not EPurged, ENoOp, ELid, ESegment). Type 1 (former EVENT_STRING) is rejected as unknown.

legacy_parts.note: Decoding of the pre-versioned 'classic' envelope (first word = event type) and of EVENT_SESSIONS_OLD (type 11) through ESessions::decode_old. Both forms were written only by C++ releases before v0.58 (commits 4123d01120f and 8e8ecb47a7c, January 2013). LogEvent::encode_with_header always writes EVENT_NEW_ENCODING, and ESessions events are created with type 12.

features.name: Legacy-format journal rewrite through the back pointer
features.summary: Rewrites a journal in an older stream format into the alternate journal inode at open time.
features.description: If the front journal's stream_format is older than `mds_journal_format`, a non-standby daemon rewrites it in `_reformat_journal`: set `back` to the other inode (`0x200+rank` and `0x300+rank` alternate) and save the pointer, create the new journal with the old layout, copy every entry (remapping offset-based segment seqs referenced by `EMetaBlob::truncate_finish`, zeroing `ESubtreeMap::expire_pos`, copying undecodable events verbatim), flush, swap front/back, erase the old journal and clear `back`. A crash leaves `back != 0`, which the next recovery cleans by erasing the journal `back` names. A standby-replay daemon tolerates an old format (and respawns with `-EAGAIN` while `back != 0`), then reformats through `MDLog::reopen` when it becomes active. A stream_format above `JOURNAL_FORMAT_MAX`, or `mds_journal_format` above it, marks the rank damaged.
features.notes: Legacy-format path only, by code reading (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 items 14, 21, 29): the pointer with the new `back` is saved before the new header is written, so a crash in that window leaves a headerless back journal and every later start of the rank goes damaged; `Journaler::flush(ctx)` can complete before the tail is durable; the new Journaler has no write-error handler until late, so a write error aborts; after `reopen()`, `append()` sets expire_pos = write_pos while replayed segments still hold dirty state. Pointer-save and erase failures `ceph_assert` (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 34). After a rewrite the active journal may stay `0x300+rank` indefinitely.

legacy.note: The rewrite runs only when the front journal's stream_format is below mds_journal_format (dev option, default 1), i.e. for format-0 journals written by C++ releases before v0.82 or created with the option set to 0. Journals created at this commit by MDLog::create and by cephfs-journal-tool journal reset use the option's default RESILIENT format, and the new MDS never opens C++ journals.

features.name: Per-rank write-ahead metadata journal with one submission order
features.summary: Every metadata mutation of a rank is logged as one event in one totally ordered stream before it counts as durable.
features.description: A mutation is applied to the cache only as a projection, journaled as a LogEvent and made real (and acknowledged as safe) only after the event is durable in RADOS. `submit_entry` (caller holds mds_lock, takes `submit_mutex`) assigns a monotonically increasing `event_seq`, attaches the event to the newest LogSegment, runs `update_segment` and queues it; the single `mds-log-submit` thread encodes events without mds_lock and appends them to the one Journaler stream, so journal order equals submission order. Submission during replay or after the log is capped is asserted against. Pending unflushed events are discarded at shutdown (clients replay unsafe requests).
features.notes: Completions must be `MDSLogContextBase` (asserted). `Journaler::append_entry` blocks the submit thread when buffered unflushed bytes would exceed `UINT_MAX - UINT_MAX>>3` (src/osdc/Journaler.cc:57). `MDLog::shutdown` joins the submit thread while holding mds_lock (that thread never takes it) and fails Journaler waiters with `-EAGAIN`. The map pages classify the one-stream-per-rank serialization as only partly inherent (mdlog-and-journaler section 6.3).

features.name: Group commit: flush and wait_for_safe
features.summary: Buffered events are written in batches when someone flushes; wait_for_safe is a barrier over everything submitted so far.
features.description: Appended entries stay in the Journaler write buffer until `MDLog::flush()`, an append that completes an object (period), or a reader of the same journal sends them; everything appended between two flushes becomes one RADOS `WRITE` per object touched. MDLog has no timer of its own: about 62 call sites flush before waiting, e.g. `Server::journal_and_reply` flushes only when no early reply was sent, and lock nudges in Locker flush. `wait_for_safe(c)` fires once every event submitted so far is durable but does not flush; callers pair it with `flush()` (Migrator export, `flush journal`, boot).
features.notes: `Journaler::flush(ctx)` completes `ctx` immediately when nothing is buffered, even if earlier flushes are still in flight (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 29). A flush issued for one request also flushes every other request's buffered events (a side effect, not a requirement).

features.name: Periodic journal flush on tick
features.summary: A tick-driven flush bounds how long an unflushed event can wait.
features.description: `MDSRankDispatcher::tick` calls `mdlog->flush()` every `mds_tick_interval` (default 5 s). This bounds the wait of events that nobody flushed, e.g. after an early reply (where `journal_and_reply` does not flush), and makes un-flushed table events (snap COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SERVER_UPDATE, client ACK) durable. The whole tick returns early while the beacon is laggy, so no periodic flush happens while the MDS cannot reach the monitors.
features.notes: The kernel comment assumes this bound: "in the worst case we must wait at most 5 seconds" (linux/fs/ceph/caps.c:2429-2431).

features.name: Ordered completions and the safe position
features.summary: Journal completions run strictly in journal order, and only over entries that are fully durable.
features.description: The Journaler advances `safe_pos` over entry boundaries as flushes commit. With several flushes in flight it moves only to the boundary recorded when the oldest outstanding flush was issued (commit d17790f299c), so a partially flushed entry is never declared safe. Waiters up to `safe_pos` are queued in offset order to the single `mds-rank-fin` finisher; `MDSLogContextBase` takes mds_lock, runs `finish` (apply projections, safe reply, cap flush ack, session reply, peer ack, table apply) and then sets `MDLog::safe_pos`, which therefore means "durable and completion executed" and is what trimming uses. Completions with `-EBLOCKLISTED`/`-ETIMEDOUT` respawn the daemon; completions are dropped once the daemon is stopping.
features.notes: The conservative rule adds up to one flush of latency under continuous load (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 9). Invariant "journal order equals projection order" is not fully guaranteed: commit fc0f61ca6ba (2026, tracker 79136) replaced an assertion in `CDir::mark_dirty` with an early return after concurrent mutations of one directory applied out of order; trigger unverified (events-and-replay section 4, I2). See also F-CLU-112 (finisher).

features.name: Safe reply only after the journal commit (early unsafe reply)
features.summary: Journal side of the safe reply: replies that report durability are sent from journal completions.
features.description: See F-NS-010 (safe reply) and F-NS-011 (early reply). Journal-side facts: for journaled mutations the safe MClientReply, cap flush acks (FLUSH_ACK, FLUSHSNAP_ACK) and session open and close replies are sent from the journal completion, after the event is durable. Clients keep requests that got only an unsafe reply and resend them with CEPH_MDS_FLAG_REPLAY; a recovering rank recognises the ones already in the journal through completed request ids (F-NS-012).
features.notes: The kernel keeps unsafe requests on `s_unsafe` until the safe reply (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:4142).

features.name: Journal prezeroing ahead of the write position
features.summary: Objects beyond the write position are deleted in advance so the recovery probe finds the true end of the journal.
features.description: Before data is flushed into a region the Journaler clears from `prezeroing_pos` up to `write_pos + journaler_prezero_periods` periods (rounded up to a period): whole periods are `DELETE`d (`Filer::zero` removes full objects), partial periods are `ZERO`ed; `-ENOENT` is success. A flush never comes closer than one period to `prezero_pos` and is held back until prezeroing catches up. After replay `trim_tail` re-runs prezeroing to overwrite bytes left after a torn tail.
features.notes: `cephfs-journal-tool journal import` also purges/zeroes trailing objects for the same reason (src/tools/cephfs/Dumper.cc:404-441).

features.name: Journal header refresh
features.summary: The header is rewritten when the journal is trimmed and periodically during flushes.
features.description: The header is written (`WRITEFULL`) after a trim pass advanced `expire_pos` (`MDLog::write_head`, only if `last_written.expire_pos < expire_pos`; optional waiters fire when that expire_pos is committed), on a Journaler flush once `journaler_write_head_interval` (15 s) passed since the last header write, and at creation, reset and reformat. Its `write_pos` is the safe position at that time, so it lags the real end. `_write_head` asserts `write_pos >= expire_pos >= trimmed_pos`, `_finish_write_head` aborts if a committed position would move backwards, and a committed header triggers object trimming.
features.notes: A freshly recovered Journaler writes its header on its first flush because `last_wrote_head` is set only by `_write_head`. With a lagging header the recovery probe may stat many objects, one period per round trip (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 11).

features.name: Journal write-error policy (damaged or respawn)
features.summary: Any journal write failure other than fencing takes the rank out of service as damaged.
features.description: Errors on a journal data write, header write, prezero or trim (for the last two, errors other than `-ENOENT`) go to the single handler `C_MDL_WriteError`: `-EBLOCKLISTED` respawns the daemon; anything else logs "Unhandled journal write error on MDS rank N: <err>, shutting down." to the cluster log and calls `damaged()`, so the rank becomes `down:damaged` until `ceph mds repaired`. `mds_action_on_write_error` does not apply to journal writes. The handler fires once per Journaler; with no handler registered the process aborts ("unhandled write error").
features.notes: `damaged()` sets the beacon want-state to down:damaged, flushes the cluster log, waits up to `mds_mon_shutdown_timeout` (5 s) and respawns. Beacon and rank states are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha ([rank lifecycle](../cpp-map/09-recovery/rank-lifecycle-and-recovery.md)).

features.name: Log segments as units of lazy writeback (segment expiry)
features.summary: Each journal segment records what its events dirtied; the segment can be dropped only after all of it is written back.
features.description: A LogSegment collects, on intrusive lists, the new and dirty dirfrags, dirty dentries and inodes, inodes with dirty backtraces or scatter state, open files, truncating and purging inodes, uncommitted leader/peer/fragment operations, pending table tids, and the InoTable/SessionMap/table versions its events produced. `LogSegment::try_to_expire` commits each dirty dirfrag (base inodes via `CInode::store`), stores backtraces batched per pool, saves InoTable, SessionMap and the snap table if newer than committed, nudges scatterlocks so their state is journaled again in a newer segment, re-journals snapshotted open files, and waits for 2PC outcomes, fragment commits, table ACKs, the OpenFileTable commit, truncates and purges; it flushes the log when it has to wait. An object is on the list of exactly one segment, the newest that dirtied it, except never-committed dirfrags, which stay in the oldest segment that mentions them until their first commit. Dirty objects hold `PIN_DIRTY`, so trimming the journal is also what lets the cache shrink.
features.notes: Replay re-dirties objects into the replayed segments, so post-recovery expiry writes them back; replay itself never writes metadata. One slow dirfrag commit, unfinished 2PC, truncate or purge blocks the whole segment and, because trimming advances only to major boundaries, every later segment up to the next major boundary (events-and-replay section 6, item 6). Dev kill points `mds_kill_journal_expire_at` 1-5 sit between the stages. See also F-CACHE-016 (cache view), F-CACHE-015 (dirty lists on cache objects).

features.name: Segment boundaries and rotation policy
features.summary: Boundary events cut the journal into minor and major segments; major ones are the only valid replay starting points.
features.description: `SegmentBoundary` events start segments: `ESubtreeMap` (2), `ELid` (101) and `EResetJournal` (9) start major segments, `ESegment` (100, body u64 seq) starts a minor one. After each submission `_segment_upkeep` submits an ESubtreeMap when more than `mds_log_minor_segments_per_major_segment` minor segments started since the last major one; otherwise an ESegment when the current segment's journaled byte range crosses an object (period) boundary or holds `mds_log_events_per_segment` or more events. `ELid` (body u64 seq) is the first event of a newly created rank (before its subtree map exists) and the last event of a stopped rank; on replay an ELid that is not the first event is skipped. Starting a segment also rotates the active stray directory index (`MDCache::advance_stray`) unless the rank is up:stopping.
features.notes: Because the counter is tested with ">", a major group is one major segment plus 17 minor segments. `ELid(seq)` constructs an event of type EVENT_SEGMENT (unused constructor). `_segment_upkeep` reads segment offsets that the submit thread writes without `submit_mutex`, so the object-boundary test lags (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 items 2, 7). Stray rotation couples stray placement to journal activity; strays are owned by 09-background-services ([strays and purge](../cpp-map/11-background-services/strays-and-purge.md)).

legacy_parts.note: The ELid(LogSegment::seq_t) constructor, which builds an event typed EVENT_SEGMENT and has no caller. Every ELid at this commit is built with the default constructor (MDSRank::boot_create, MDCache::shutdown_pass, LogEvent::decode_event, ELid::generate_test_instances).

features.name: Background journal trimming with throttle
features.summary: A trim thread expires old segments whenever the journal exceeds its segment or event budget.
features.description: The `mds-log-trim` thread runs `MDLog::trim` every `mds_log_trim_upkeep_interval` (1000 ms) while the rank is up:active or up:stopping, holding mds_lock for the pass. It starts expiring the oldest segments that have no pending events and `end <= safe_pos` while non-expiring segments exceed `mds_log_max_segments` or events exceed `mds_log_max_events`, starting at most `mds_log_trim_threshold` segments per decay window (decaying counter, half-life `mds_log_trim_decay_rate`). Writeback op priority rises from `CEPH_MSG_PRIO_LOW` (64) to `CEPH_MSG_PRIO_HIGH` (196) with the expiring backlog. Each pass ends with an OpenFileTable commit attempt and `_trim_expired_segments`. When the cache is read-only (after a metadata write error with the default policy) trim and `_maybe_expired` return immediately, so the journal grows until MDS_TRIM.
features.notes: `MDLog::handle_conf_change` updates cached values, but `mds_log_warn_factor` and `mds_log_minor_segments_per_major_segment` are absent from `get_tracked_keys` (which lists a non-existent `mds_log_major_segment_event_ratio`), so runtime changes of those two do not reach MDLog (src/mds/MDSRank.cc:4188-4197; mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 5).

features.name: Major-group trimming and journal object deletion
features.summary: Expired segments are dropped only up to a major boundary, then whole journal objects behind it are deleted.
features.description: `_trim_expired_segments` deletes expired segments only in whole groups ending right before a major segment and sets the Journaler `expire_pos` to the start of that major boundary, so the on-disk journal always begins at a major boundary and the newest segment is never deleted. MDLog then writes the header; only after a header recording the new `expire_pos` has committed does `Journaler::_trim` `DELETE` whole objects below it (rounded down to a period) via `Filer::purge_range`, one purge at a time with `filer_max_purge_ops` (10) removes in flight. `trimmed_pos` reaches disk only with the next header write. Expired segments can stay in memory until the next major boundary is fully reached, which is why the MDS often sits a little above `mds_log_max_segments`.
features.notes: Durability invariant: on disk `expire_pos >= trimmed_pos`, i.e. objects are deleted only after a header with a later expire_pos is durable (src/osdc/Journaler.cc:1387). The header's `trimmed_pos` lags deletions, so a standby-replay follower can read an already deleted object, get `-ENOENT` and respawn (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 12).

features.name: flush journal admin command
features.summary: Admin command that writes back every dirty object and trims the journal to a fresh major segment.
features.description: asok/tell `flush journal` (`C_Flush_Journal`) returns `-EROFS` when read-only and is a no-op returning 0 unless up:active. Otherwise it submits a fresh ESubtreeMap, flushes and waits for safe, expires every older segment with `trim_to`, waits for all expiring segments, trims and answers when the header with the new `expire_pos` is committed. Thereby every dirty dirfrag, backtrace, base inode, InoTable, SessionMap, snap table and OpenFileTable entry is written to RADOS. Output: `{"message": ..., "return_code": N}` with rc = return_code; errors read "Error <r> (<str>) while flushing journal|trimming log|writing header" (`trim_to` can return `-EAGAIN`). `cache drop` (F-ADM-044) runs the same state machine after recalling client state.
features.notes: Runbooks rely on it: src/tools/cephfs/first-damage.py:16 instructs `ceph tell mds.<fs_name>:0 flush journal` before scanning. `trim_to(seq)` ignores its argument whenever segments exist and `trim_all()` with no segment asserts (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 4); unlike `trim()`, `trim_to` does not check for a read-only cache. The admin command framework is owned by 11-security-admin-and-observability ([admin commands](../cpp-map/13-admin-and-config/admin-commands.md)). Documented operator step before offline repair (`flush journal`, `fs fail`, journal tool) and heavily used by qa (e.g. `test_volumes.py` before `dump inode`). Command plane: F-ADM-040.

features.name: Journal capping when a rank stops
features.summary: A stopping rank writes everything back, trims its journal to a final ELid and refuses further events.
features.description: In up:stopping, after subtrees are exported, strays migrated and sessions closed, `MDCache::shutdown_pass` journals an ESubtreeMap if the current segment has more than one event or dirty dirfrags, calls `trim_all` every tick until at most one segment remains, then submits `ELid`, flushes and caps the log (`MDLog::cap`). From then on `submit_entry` asserts, OpenFileTable commits stop and the current segment may be expired. A cleanly stopped rank leaves a journal whose `expire_pos` points at that ELid; when the rank is started again (up:starting) it appends after it without replay.
features.notes: up:stopping -> down:stopped requires the log to be trimmed and capped; rank states are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha ([rank lifecycle](../cpp-map/09-recovery/rank-lifecycle-and-recovery.md)). Stopped ranks keep all their objects (journal, tables, mdsdir, strays); no code deletes them (rados-object-catalog section 8). After `cap()`, `try_to_expire` asserts `!is_capped()` if open files remain in a segment.

features.name: EMetaBlob after-image container
features.summary: The container embedded in most events that carries complete new images of every touched dirfrag, dentry and inode.
features.description: `EMetaBlob` (`ENCODE_START(8,5)`) holds, in encode order: lump_order and a map of per-dirfrag lumps, base-inode images (`roots`), `table_tids`, `opened_ino`, ino allocation fields (`allocated_ino`, `used_preallocated_ino`, `preallocated_inos`, `client_name`, `inotablev`, `sessionmapv`), `truncate_start`, `truncate_finish`, `destroyed_inodes`, `client_reqs`, `renamed_dirino` and `renamed_dir_frags`, a legacy placeholder (int64 -1, bool false) and `client_flushes`. A `dirlump` (2,2) holds the full `fnode_t`, state flags (COMPLETE, DIRTY, NEW, IMPORTING, DIRTYDFT) and lazily decoded lists of `fullbit` (9,5: dentry name, first/last, version, full `inode_t`, xattrs, symlink, dirfragtree, snap blob, old_inodes, oldest_snap, alternate_name, flags DIRTY/DIRTYPARENT/DIRTYPOOL/NEED_SNAPFLUSH/EPHEMERAL_RANDOM), `remotebit` (3,2) and `nullbit` (2,2). Images are taken from projected state and are complete after-images, never field deltas or RADOS-level records; the submit thread encodes them off-lock because the blob holds only immutable snapshots.
features.notes: cephfs-journal-tool uses `EMetaBlob::get_inodes/get_dentries/get_paths/dump` for filters and `recover_dentries` writes fullbits back into dirfrag objects. Cost: a one-byte setattr journals the full inode plus parent dirfrag and ancestor images; `EImportStart` journals a whole subtree. The decoder still accepts v1-v7. `dirlump::_encode_bits` appends to a cached buffer when a decoded lump is re-encoded (events-and-replay section 8).

legacy_parts.note: The EMetaBlob::decode branches for struct_v 1-7 ('The decoder still accepts v1-v7'): roots as a bufferlist before v4, client_reqs without tids before v2, no renamed_dirino before v3, no client_flushes before v8. Struct versions below 8 were written only by C++ releases before v9.1.0 (v8 added client_flushes, commit 2d6ab6e53b8, 2015), and the encoder at this commit writes ENCODE_START(8, 5). The int64 -1 / bool false placeholder is still written by the current encoder and belongs to the current format.

features.name: EMetaBlob path context and ancestor images
features.summary: Rules that decide which ancestor dentries and inodes each event must carry so replay can attach it to the tree.
features.description: `add_dir_context` walks from a dirfrag toward the root and adds clean ancestor dentries before the dirfrag's lump. In the default mode the ancestors of a directory inode journaled since the last major segment (`CInode::last_journaled`) are treated as optional and dropped when the walk reaches an unambiguous auth subtree root of this rank; this is safe only because the journal is always trimmed to a major boundary. `TO_ROOT` mode (ESubtreeMap, EExport base) records full paths. Lump-order invariant: the lump holding a directory's fullbit precedes the directory's dirfrag lump; otherwise replay marks the rank damaged. In addition `predirty_journal_parents` projects and journals the parent dirfrag and every ancestor inode into which it propagates fragstat/rstat (stopping at non-auth or unlockable parents or within `mds_dirstat_min_interval`), so each mutation carries full ancestor images.
features.notes: Statistic semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes ([rstats](../cpp-map/10-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes/rstats-quotas-and-subvolumes.md)); this entry covers only what lands in the journal. Only the topmost projected dirfrag is added as a dirty lump, so replay rebuilds dirty scatter state only at the propagation stop point.

features.name: Snapshot COW images in the journal
features.summary: When a snapshot intervenes, events also carry the old (snapshotted) dentry and inode versions.
features.description: `MDCache::journal_cow_dentry` adds the old dentry/inode for `[first, follows]` to the blob when a snapshot intervenes: a snapped primary dentry with its own inode copy for plain files, or `old_inodes` in the head inode for multiversion inodes, plus a snapped remote dentry when such an inode is renamed or unlinked. Snapshotted inodes that still need a client snapflush are flagged NEED_SNAPFLUSH and put on the segment's open_files. Replay identifies dentries by (dir, name, last) and inodes by (ino, last), so COW copies coexist with the head (last = CEPH_NOSNAP).
features.notes: Snapshot semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes ([snapshots](../cpp-map/10-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes/snapshots.md)). See also F-SNAP-026.

features.name: ESubtreeMap: major boundary with the subtree map
features.summary: The replay starting point: which subtrees the rank owns, plus the tree path to each of them.
features.description: `ESubtreeMap` (type 2, `ENCODE_START(6,5)`): stamp, an EMetaBlob with TO_ROOT context and a clean lump for every own subtree root and bound plus mydir, `map<dirfrag, vector<dirfrag>> subtrees` (root to bounds; nested own non-ambiguous subtrees are swallowed), `ambiguous_subtrees` (v>=4), `expire_pos` (v>=3) and `seq` (v>=6). `MDCache::create_subtree_map` builds it under mds_lock and submit_mutex at every major rotation, at boot (creating, starting), on `flush journal` and on stop. The first one replayed into an empty cache replays its metablob and installs subtree authority (ambiguous imports become (me,me) and are registered for resolve); later ones only cross-check the cache and skip their metablob. Replay raises the in-memory expire_pos to the recorded value.
features.notes: Always-fatal cross-check: replay ends with `ceph_assert(!get_debug_subtrees() || errors == 0)`, but `MDLog::get_debug_subtrees()` returns `events_per_segment` (min 1) since commit 218bdb66d27e, so any mismatch between a later subtree map and the cache aborts the daemon (not `damaged()`) regardless of `mds_debug_subtrees` (src/mds/journal.cc:2936-2941). The event grows with the subtree count and its replay holds mds_lock throughout. `cephfs-journal-tool header recover` searches for the first SUBTREEMAP/SUBTREEMAP_TEST/LID/RESETJOURNAL. See also F-CACHE-036 (subtree map).

features.name: EUpdate: generic mutation record
features.summary: The event most client requests and internal mutations are journaled as.
features.description: `EUpdate` (type 20, `ENCODE_START(4,4)`): stamp, a free-form `type` label, metablob, `client_map` (sessions force-opened by cap import, as an encoded bufferlist) with `cmapv` (v>=3), `reqid` and `had_peers`. Emitted by openc, setattr, open_truncate, setlayout and layout vxattrs, setxattr/removexattr, mknod, mkdir, symlink, link, unlink, rename, snapshot ops and quarantine flags (Server), by cap update, snap flush, check_inode_max_size and scatter writebehind (Locker), scatter stat updates (CInode), purge_stray (StrayManager) and create system file, cow, truncate finish, uninline and repair_dirfrag (MDCache). Replay replays the metablob, registers an uncommitted leader when `had_peers`, and replays `client_map` sessions if the session map is older than `cmapv`.
features.notes: Replay never interprets the label; cephfs-journal-tool only prints it, and its `--type` filter matches the event type id, not this label (src/tools/cephfs/JournalFilter.cc:65-69).

features.name: EOpen: open-file journaling
features.summary: Keeps opened and snapshot-flush-pending inodes inside the untrimmed journal so replay brings them into cache.
features.description: `EOpen` (type 22, `ENCODE_START(4,3)`, decoder declares 3): stamp, a metablob with clean images of the open inodes and their path context, `inos`, `snap_inos` (v>=4). Written by `Server::handle_client_open` and `Locker::adjust_cap_wanted` only when the OpenFileTable says it is still needed, by `Locker::check_inode_max_size` instead of an EUpdate when caps are wanted, and by segment expiry for snapshotted inodes with client snap caps (pending snapflush), which are re-journaled in the current segment and waited for before the old segment expires. Replay puts the listed inodes on the segment's open_files (asserting they are cached); head inodes are dropped from those lists at active_start because the OpenFileTable tracks them.
features.notes: `EOpen::update_segment` is empty. `openfiles ls` shows these segment lists, not the OpenFileTable (mds-tables G17).

features.name: Session events: ESession and ESessions
features.summary: Journal records of session open, close and force-open, with the inode numbers released or to purge.
features.description: `ESession` (type 10, `ENCODE_START(7,5)`): stamp, client_inst, open flag, `cmapv`, `inos_to_free`, `inotablev`, `client_metadata` (v>=5), `inos_to_purge` (v>=6), `auth_name` (v>=7). A session open is journaled after `mark_projected`, and the `CEPH_SESSION_OPEN` reply is sent only when the event is safe; close/kill/evict journals `inos_to_free` (pending + free preallocated numbers) and `inos_to_purge` (delegated numbers). `ESessions` (type 12, (2,1); legacy unversioned type 11) and the `client_map` carried by EUpdate (rename importing caps) or EImportStart record sessions force-opened because another rank handed over caps (`prepare_force_open_sessions` skips blocklisted clients). Replay creates or removes sessions under version gating, restoring client_metadata and filling auth_name if absent.
features.notes: Ganesha reclaim checks `auth_name` equality (`-EPERM` otherwise), which survives failover through ESession v7 (src/mds/Server.cc:476-521). A replayed close for an unknown session logs "replayed stray Session close event" and is ignored. Session semantics are owned by 02-client-sessions-and-protocol ([sessions](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/sessions.md)). See also F-PROTO-028 (session open handshake).

legacy_parts.note: Decoding of type 11 (EVENT_SESSIONS_OLD) as an unversioned ESessions ('legacy unversioned type 11'). Type 11 was written only by C++ releases before v0.58 (commit 8e8ecb47a7c, 2013). ESessions at this commit are journaled as type 12 with ENCODE_START(2, 1).

features.name: Completed client request ids in journal and SessionMap
features.summary: Journal side of the completed-request table.
features.description: See F-NS-012. Journal-side facts: every client request journaled through an EUpdate carries client_reqs (metareqid, oldest_client_tid) in its EMetaBlob; replay inserts the tid into the session's completed_requests with the created inode number (allocated or preallocated; asserted single when an inode was created) and trims by oldest_client_tid; completed_requests are also persisted in the session's SessionMap value (save_if_dirty at expiry). A request whose entry never reached the journal is re-executed, reusing head.ino.
features.notes: Opens journaled as EOpen and internal mutations carry no client_reqs. Replay sets only `completed_requests_dirty` and never fills `touched_sessions`, so replayed records reach the sessionmap object only through `dirty_sessions` or a later live segment; whether two consecutive failovers can lose them is unverified (events-and-replay section 8).

features.name: Completed cap flush ids in journal and SessionMap
features.summary: Journal side of cap flush idempotency.
features.description: See F-CAPS-019. Journal-side facts: cap update and snap flush EUpdates record client_flushes (metareqid, oldest_flush_tid) when the client sends a non-zero oldest_flush_tid (EMetaBlob v8); replay rebuilds the session's completed_flushes and trims by oldest_flush_tid; the set is also persisted in session_info_t (F-STORE-075).
features.notes: The kernel encodes `oldest_flush_tid` in cap messages (linux/fs/ceph/caps.c:1348).

features.name: Destroyed inode records
features.summary: Marks inodes deleted for good so replay and the open-file prefetch forget them.
features.description: Stray purge completion (`StrayManager::_purge_stray_purged`, after the PurgeQueue entry is durable) journals the inode in EMetaBlob `destroyed_inodes`. Replay removes the inode from the cache if present (asserting its parent dentry is null) and records the numbers per segment with `OpenFileTable::note_destroyed_inos`, so the rejoin prefetch skips numbers that may still appear in an older OpenFileTable commit.
features.notes: A standby-replay daemon trims this map with a journal byte offset although its keys are segment seqs (mds-tables G15, code reading). Purge is owned by 09-background-services ([strays and purge](../cpp-map/11-background-services/strays-and-purge.md)). See also F-BG-014 (durable purge intent).

features.name: Cross-rank two-phase-commit records
features.summary: Leader and peer journal records that let multi-rank link, unlink and rename survive a crash of either side.
features.description: Peers journal `EPeerUpdate` (type 21, (3,3): stamp, type label, reqid, leader rank, op PREPARE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, origop LINK/RENAME/RMDIR, `commit` EMetaBlob, `rollback` bufferlist); the leader journals one EUpdate with `had_peers` and, after every peer reported OP_COMMITTED, `ECommitted` (type 23, reqid). Rollback blobs are logical undo records: `link_rollback`, `rmdir_rollback`, `rename_rollback` (3,2) with `drec` (2,2) entries. Uncommitted leader and peer operations pin their segments. Replay rebuilds `uncommitted_leaders` (safe, empty peer set) and `uncommitted_peers` (keeping unlinked inodes and old subtree roots cached) for resolve, which journals the outcome (OP_COMMIT "unknown", rollback, or ECommitted).
features.notes: A rename prepare whose blob is empty, or an rmdir prepare on a peer that owns no subtree-root dirfrag of the directory, is not journaled and the ack is marked "not journaled"; link prepares are always journaled. Resolve is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha ([resolve and rejoin](../cpp-map/09-recovery/resolve-and-rejoin.md)); the 2PC message exchange by 07-multi-mds.

features.name: Subtree migration records and rename subtree hints
features.summary: Journal records that make subtree export/import and directory renames across subtrees recoverable.
features.description: The importer journals `EImportStart` (type 4: stamp, base, a metablob with every imported dirfrag and dentry with dirty flags preserved, bounds, `cmapv` + `client_map` of force-opened sessions, from rank) before acking, then `EImportFinish` (type 5, success flag) when the export finishes or reverses; the exporter journals `EExport` (type 3: metablob with TO_ROOT context, base, bounds, target) only after the importer's ack. An EImportStart without finish leaves the subtree ambiguous ((me,me)) for resolve, which journals the EImportFinish; an EImportFinish with no pending import marks the rank damaged. EMetaBlob `renamed_dirino` and `renamed_dir_frags` let replay adjust the subtree map after directory renames and open non-auth bounds of an imported renamed directory.
features.notes: EImportStart can exceed `mds_log_event_large_threshold` and its replay holds mds_lock throughout. At most one null dentry per blob is allowed when renamed_dirino is set (asserted). Migration is owned by 07-multi-mds ([subtree migration](../cpp-map/08-multi-mds/subtree-migration.md)). See also F-MULTI-021 (migration ordering).

features.name: EFragment journal protocol and old dirfrag object cleanup
features.summary: Journal records and object operations that make a directory split or merge crash-safe.
features.description: `EFragment` (type 6, (5,4): stamp, op PREPARE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/FINISH, ino, basefrag, bits (> 0 split, < 0 merge), metablob, orig_frags, rollback with one `dirfrag_rollback{fnode}` per original frag in PREPARE). After PREPARE the new frags are committed in full; then COMMIT; then old frag objects are `DELETE`d, except `frag_t()`, which gets `TRUNCATE 0` + `OMAP_CLEAR` to keep its backtrace/layout xattrs (results other than 0 or `-ENOENT` assert); then FINISH. Replay tracks uncommitted fragments; at resolve or reconnect start `reopen_log` re-runs old-object cleanup for committed ones and rolls back prepared-only ones (journaling ROLLBACK, restoring fnodes, removing new objects); rejoin_done waits until none remain.
gates: mds_debug_frag (dev: verify dirfrags after EFragment replay)
features.notes: Split/merge policy and cache-side mechanics are owned by 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags ([dirfrags](../cpp-map/04-cache/dirfrags-and-fragmentation.md)). The OSD returns -ENOENT for remove and omap_clear on a missing object without creating it, so repeating the purge is safe. See also F-CACHE-087 (fragment operation), F-CACHE-089 (cache side), F-CACHE-094 (recovery of in-flight operations).

features.name: Journal open and recovery thread
features.summary: Finds, validates and if necessary repairs the rank's journal before replay or append.
features.description: `MDLog::open` starts `mds-log-recvr`, which works with blocking I/O and without mds_lock: declares damage if `mds_journal_format` exceeds `JOURNAL_FORMAT_MAX`; loads or creates the journal pointer; if `back != 0` recovers and erases the back journal (standby-replay: `-EAGAIN`, respawn); recovers the front journal (header read and forward probe); rejects an unknown stream_format as damaged and reformats an older one; installs the journal write-error handler. `-EBLOCKLISTED` respawns; other errors call `damaged_unlocked()`. `MDLog::reopen` runs the same recovery again (thread `mds-log-reopen`) for a former standby-replay daemon that tolerated an old format.
features.notes: The code comments that `Journaler::recover` succeeds when no objects exist, but a missing header object yields `-ENOENT` and the rank goes damaged, also for a back journal whose header was never written; the clog message in that branch names `jp.front` although it recovers `jp.back` (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 14). A fresh Journaler with an empty header object reaches ACTIVE with stream_format -1, which is rejected as unknown (damaged).

legacy_parts.note: Recovery and erase of a back journal left by an interrupted rewrite (and the -EAGAIN respawn of standby-replay in that case), the hand-off to _reformat_journal for stream formats older than mds_journal_format, and MDLog::reopen (thread mds-log-reopen) for a former standby-replay daemon that tolerated an old format. These branches act only on journals in format 0 or left mid-rewrite, i.e. data from C++ releases before v0.82 or from the dev option mds_journal_format = 0. MDLog::reopen's only caller is the reformat check in MDSRank::replay_done. The pointer load, front-journal recovery, the unknown-format check and the write-error handler are current.

features.name: End-of-journal probe and torn-tail handling
features.summary: Determines where the journal really ends after a crash and discards a partially written last entry.
features.description: `Journaler::recover` reads the header, sets all positions from it, then probes forward from the header `write_pos`: `Filer::probe` `STAT`s every object of one period at a time (`RWORDERED`, `-ENOENT` = size 0) until the first object shorter than its extent; the first round covers the rest of the current period plus one more. The probed end becomes write_pos. While reading, if the next entry is incomplete and all data up to write_pos has been received, the Journaler rewinds write_pos, flush_pos, safe_pos and prezero_pos to the entry start and reports end of journal; the bytes remain until `trim_tail` (prezeroing) overwrites them after replay. Because safe_pos never passes an uncommitted flush, out-of-order commits across objects can only lose the unsafe tail.
features.notes: Correct only because prezeroing removes objects ahead of the write position. `_finish_probe_end` aborts on an impossible end of -1. The torn tail is silently discarded ("FIXME: truncate on disk?", mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 10).

features.name: Journal replay pipeline
features.summary: Reads the journal from the last major boundary and applies every event to rebuild the rank's state.
features.description: `MDLog::replay` (journaler active and read-only) starts `mds-log-replay`. It reads entries from `expire_pos` to the probed end, prefetching `journaler_prefetch_periods` periods with `FADVISE_DONTNEED` reads that never pass safe_pos, and decodes each without mds_lock. Every boundary event creates a LogSegment (seq from the event, or the byte offset when the seq is 0); events before the first major boundary are refused; then each event's `replay(mds)` runs under mds_lock, one at a time, in journal order. Replay never writes metadata to RADOS: it rebuilds the cache, subtree map, sessions, tables and recovery queues and re-dirties objects into the replayed segments. At the end it asserts `read_pos == write_pos`; a non-standby rank then makes the journal writeable, zeroes after a torn tail and moves to resolve, or to reconnect when it is the only in rank and none failed.
features.notes: Fully sequential: an EImportStart or ESubtreeMap with thousands of items holds mds_lock for its whole replay (heartbeat reset every `mds_heartbeat_reset_grace` items). No event can be journaled during replay, so recovery work that must journal (2PC outcomes, fragment rollback, import disambiguation, ECommitted) waits until resolve or later. Oversized entries extend the read window temporarily.

features.name: Cache reconstruction from after-images
features.summary: How replay turns EMetaBlob images back into cache objects, linkage and dirty state.
features.description: `EMetaBlob::replay` installs base-inode images, then processes lumps in `lump_order`: `get_force_dirfrag` (refragmenting cached frags to match; a missing directory inode other than another rank's `~mdsN` marks the rank damaged), `reset_fnode`, then all fullbits (find or create the inode by (ino, last), unlink what the dentry pointed to, relink, mark dirty and dirty-parent), all remotebits and all nullbits. It then adjusts subtrees after directory renames, removes truly unlinked inodes, and applies table tids, opened_ino, InoTable/SessionMap changes, truncates, destroyed inodes and completed request/flush ids. Images are installed without version comparison (the last image wins); dirty lumps rebuild scatter-dirty state; dirfrags not marked complete stay incomplete, and when fetched later cached (journal) dentries take precedence over on-disk ones.
features.notes: A regular file without a valid layout or with pool_id -1 marks the rank damaged; an alternate_name mismatch on an existing dentry asserts; a dentry linked to the wrong inode logs "FIXME had dentry linked to wrong inode" and is relinked (the journal wins) (events-and-replay section 8).

features.name: Version-gated redo of table operations
features.summary: Table changes are journaled as versioned operations and re-applied only if the stored table is older.
features.description: InoTable, SessionMap and SnapServer changes are journaled as operations carrying the table version reached after them; each operation bumps the version by exactly one, live and at replay, so one event may advance a table by more than one (a create that takes an InoTable number and refills the session preallocation is +2 InoTable, +1 SessionMap). Replay applies an event only if the loaded object (`mds<r>_inotable`, `mds<r>_sessionmap`, `mds_snaptable`) is older: ESession requires exactly version+1 (a gap wipes all sessions if `mds_wipe_sessions`, otherwise asserts), ETableServer requires `version - 1 == table version`, EMetaBlob applies its allocations and force-repairs a remaining shortfall with a clog error, and `replay_open_sessions` tolerates sessions already saved. Consequently table objects are always at or behind the journal and replay never needs to read dirfrags.
features.notes: Completed request/flush ids are not versioned; they are inserted unconditionally into whatever session exists and dropped if the session is gone.

features.name: Replay error policy and the damaged rank
features.summary: What happens when the journal cannot be read or decoded: the rank is reported damaged, or a standby respawns.
features.description: A missing journal object (`-ENOENT`): clog "missing journal object" and damaged (standby-replay: `-EAGAIN`, respawn). `-EINVAL` (short read or bad framing): the header is re-read; standby-replay gets `-EAGAIN`, otherwise damaged. An undecodable event: clog "corrupt journal event at <pos>~<len> / <write_pos>" plus a hex dump, then damaged unless `mds_log_skip_corrupt_events`; events before the first major boundary: damaged unless `mds_log_skip_unbounded_events`. Other replay inconsistencies (missing dir inode, invalid layout, unknown table op, EImportFinish without import) also call `damaged()`, which requests `down:damaged` from the monitor and respawns; the rank stays damaged until `ceph mds repaired`. `boot_start` maps `-EAGAIN` in standby-replay to respawn, `-EINVAL`/`-ENOENT` to damaged, `-EROFS` to continue read-only, anything else to suicide.
features.notes: Assertion failures (subtree-map mismatch, trailing bytes after an event, start_ptr mismatch) crash the daemon instead; the monitor handles that as an ordinary daemon failure, not as down:damaged. Skipping silently loses the skipped metadata updates. The `-EINVAL` path calls `standby_trim_segments` on the replay thread without mds_lock (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 27).

features.name: Post-replay session and InoTable consistency check
features.summary: Detects preallocated inode numbers that the InoTable still lists as free after replay.
features.description: After every replay pass (standby-replay passes included) `validate_sessions` asserts for each session that `prealloc_inos == free_prealloc_inos`, and if any preallocated number is still free in the InoTable logs "loaded with preallocated inodes that are inconsistent with inotable" and calls `damaged()`.

features.name: Single-writer fencing before reading rank state
features.summary: What the OSDs guarantee once a replacement has waited for the fencing epoch.
features.description: See F-CLU-037 (the wait) and F-CLU-036 (the blocklist). Storage-side facts: the OSDMap with the blocklist commits in the same or an earlier Paxos round than the FSMap that records last_failure_osd_epoch; replay_start waits for an OSDMap at least that new before reading the journal pointer, tables, sessionmap or journal. An OSD PG processes an op only once it has the op's map epoch and rejects later ops of the old instance with -EBLOCKLISTED, so the journal and backing objects have exactly one writer.
features.notes: Gaps by code reading (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 items 13, 24, 30): `wait_for_map` waits for the monitor's latest committed version and does not re-check the target, so a lagging monitor could answer below it (unverified); `FSMap::erase` overwrites the per-filesystem `last_failure_osd_epoch` with 0 when a standby-replay daemon is removed in the same pending map, so a replacement can skip the wait; up:starting and up:creating never wait.

features.name: Standby-replay journal tailing (journal side)
features.summary: Journal side of standby-replay tailing.
features.description: See F-CLU-068 (follower loop) and F-CLU-069 (takeover). Journal-side facts: the follower runs the same replay code read-only; journal -ENOENT/-EINVAL map to -EAGAIN (respawn), and a journal being rewritten (pointer back != 0) also makes it respawn. After promotion the final pass re-reads head and probe, opens the PurgeQueue and OpenFileTable, replays the remainder, then reformats an old-format journal, makes it writeable and trims the tail.
features.notes: `reread_head_and_probe` asserts on any error except `-EBLOCKLISTED`, so a missing or corrupt header crashes the follower. `standby_trim_segments` never prunes `major_segments`, so the `segmjr` gauge grows on a long-running follower (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 28).

legacy_parts.note: The respawn while the journal pointer has back != 0 (journal being rewritten) and the reformat of an old-format journal after promotion. Both steps occur only for journals in format 0 or left mid-rewrite (C++ releases before v0.82, or the dev option mds_journal_format = 0).

features.name: Journal creation and append-only open per rank state
features.summary: How the journal is created for a new rank and reopened without replay for a cleanly stopped one.
features.description: up:creating: `MDLog::create` makes a Journaler on `0x200+rank` with all positions at one period, writes the header and the pointer `{0x200+rank, 0}` asynchronously and starts the submit thread; the rank then submits `ELid` (first, major segment), builds its hierarchy dirty in that segment, journals an ESubtreeMap and waits for it to be safe before `creating_done`. up:starting (a previously stopped rank): open, then `append()` sets read_pos = expire_pos = write_pos without replay, journals a fresh ESubtreeMap, flushes and waits for safe before `starting_done`. up:replay: replay, then reformat if needed, `set_writeable`, `trim_tail`. up:resolve and up:reconnect call `reopen_log`, which despite its name only rolls back uncommitted fragment operations.
features.notes: The monitor decides creating vs starting vs replay (src/mds/FSMap.cc:1036-1046); rank states are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha. See also F-CLU-064 (up:creating), F-CLU-065 (up:starting), F-CLU-063 (boot stages).

legacy_parts.note: The 'reformat if needed' step of up:replay before set_writeable. The reformat runs only when the replayed journal's stream_format is below mds_journal_format, i.e. for format-0 journals (C++ releases before v0.82 or the dev option set to 0).

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Metadata object naming and placement
features.summary: Every MDS metadata object has a computed name in the metadata pool; there is no index.
features.description: All MDS metadata objects live in the file system's metadata pool, default namespace (locators are built from the pool id only). Names are computed: `"%llx.%08llx"` of (inode number, object number or raw 32-bit `frag_t`) for dirfrags and journals, `"%llx.%08llx.inode"` for base inodes, `"mds%d_inotable"`, `"mds%d_sessionmap"`, `"mds%d_openfiles.%x"` per rank and `"mds_snaptable"` for the global table. A `frag_t` has the bit count in its upper 8 bits and the value in the most significant bits of the lower 24 (unsplit frag = `0x00000000`). No index of dirfrags or data objects exists: existence is implied by inode metadata (fragtree, size, layout), and offline tools rediscover structure by listing pools and parsing names.
features.notes: first-damage.py selects objects by name regex and cephfs-data-scan `scan_frags` by ino >= 2^40 (rados-object-catalog section 3.15). `frag_t::decode` silently corrects a byte-swapped frag (tracker 73792). Operator procedures (doc/cephfs/disaster-recovery-experts.rst) name `mds0_inotable`, `mds0_sessionmap`, `mds_snaptable` directly.

legacy_parts.note: frag_t::decode silently correcting byte-swapped frag_t values (tracker 73792), named in the notes. Byte-swapped frag_t values were written by Ceph C++ code on big-endian hosts before commit 9e3837c837b (first in v21.0.0, backported to 19.2.7 and 20.2.1). frag_t::encode at this commit writes little-endian on every host.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Special inode numbers and per-rank ranges
features.summary: Fixed inode numbers for root and per-rank system objects, and the 2^40-wide user range of each rank.
features.description: `1` root, `2` legacy `.ceph` (not created since v0.79, commit 81bcf43080a; may exist on older file systems), `3` global snaprealm (in memory only), `4` lost+found (created only by cephfs-data-scan), `0x100+r` mdsdir, `0x200+r` journal, `0x300+r` alternate journal, `0x400+r` journal pointer, `0x500+r` purge queue, `0x600+10r+i` stray dirs (i = 0..9), `0x1000` system base; numbers `0x1000 .. 2^40-1` are never allocated; rank r allocates user inodes from `[(r+1)<<40, (r+2)<<40)`. `MAX_MDS` = `0x100`. `LOOKUPINO` on `[0x100, 0x1000)` returns `-ESTALE`. The kernel hard-codes the same private range (`ceph_vino_is_reserved` -> `-EREMOTEIO`, NFS handle decode skips them); both clients treat inode 1 as the mount root and inode 3 as the global realm.
features.notes: libcephfs refuses `[0x100, 0x1000)` in `_lookup_vino` with `-ESTALE` (src/client/Client.cc:192-198). Offline tools derive the owning table with `rank = (ino >> 40) - 1` (src/tools/cephfs/DataScan.cc:1495-1514). The rank only selects the allocator; an inode keeps its number when its subtree migrates. CInode::is_system() is ino < 0x1000 and MDS_IS_PRIVATE_INO is [0x100, 0x1000); the legacy .ceph inode (2) is skipped by readdir and never fragmented; lost+found (4) is reserved for recovery tools. The kernel also ignores delegated ranges starting below 0x1000 and warns (rate-limited) for reserved inos >= 0x200; it mounts by GETATTR relative to CEPH_INO_ROOT and ino 3 reaches clients as a snaprealm ino. See also F-PROTO-100 (ranges clients accept), F-CACHE-003 (refusals on private inodes), F-STORE-069 (InoTable).

legacy_parts.note: Ino 2 (/.ceph): its skip in readdir and snapdiff listings and its exclusion from fragmentation; and 0x300+rank, used only by the legacy-format journal rewrite. /.ceph exists only on file systems created by C++ releases before v0.79 (commit 81bcf43080a stopped creating it), and MDS_INO_LOG_BACKUP_OFFSET (0x300) is referenced only by _reformat_journal. The other fixed numbers and the per-rank ranges are current.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Dirfrag omap object and fnode header
features.summary: Each directory fragment is one omap object whose header holds the fragment's statistics and version.
features.description: Directory fragment objects are `<dirino>.<frag>` in the metadata pool. The omap header is `fnode_t` `ENCODE_START(4,3)`{u64 version, snap_purged_thru, fragstat, accounted_fragstat (`frag_info_t` (3,2)), rstat, accounted_rstat (`nest_info_t` (3,2)), u32 damage_flags (v3), recursive/localized scrub versions and stamps (v4)}; there is one omap key per non-null dentry. The header must decode completely or the frag is treated as damaged; an empty header (object missing, or an object holding only backtrace xattrs) is reported as "object missing on disk". Non-base inodes have no object of their own: they are embedded in the dentry value. The `frag_t()` object exists once the directory has a backtrace and keeps the `parent`/`layout` xattrs even when it is no longer a leaf.
gates: MDSMap incompat features 4 "dir inode in separate object" and 6 "dirfrag is stored in omap"
features.notes: `fnode.version` is adopted on load only if the in-memory CDir has version 0. `damage_flags` is never interpreted by the MDS; cephfs-data-scan sets it by OR-ing the enum values DAMAGE_STATS=0, RSTATS=1, FRAGTREE=2 as if they were bits. Readers and writers outside the MDS: cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-meta-injection, first-damage.py.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Dentry omap keys, including snapshotted dentries
features.summary: Key format of dentries in dirfrag objects, with one extra key per snapshotted version.
features.description: Key `<name>_head` for a live dentry and `<name>_<last snapid in hex>` for each COWed version still covering a live snapshot (the value's `first` gives `[first, last]`); decode splits at the last `_` and asserts (daemon abort) when there is none. Null dentries are never stored: unlinking a name removes its key. The name is what the client sent: the folded name for charmap directories, the base64 ciphertext (long names truncated plus SHA-256) for fscrypt, with the original in `alternate_name`. Stray dentries are named by hex inode number; the mdsdir holds `stray0_head` .. `stray9_head`. When `fnode.snap_purged_thru` is below the realm's `last_destroyed`, snapped keys whose range contains no live snapshot are skipped on load and removed by the next commit.
features.notes: `mds_bal_fragment_size_max` bounds only head dentries, so a dirfrag with many snapshotted keys can exceed the OSD LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS threshold (200000 keys). first-damage.py reads the first 8 bytes (`first`) of every value. No MRemoveSnaps is sent for the metadata pool; snapshot metadata is these omap keys.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Primary dentry value with embedded inode (InodeStore)
features.summary: An inode's whole persistent state lives in the omap value of its primary dentry.
features.description: Value = u64 `first` + `'i'` + `ENCODE_START(2,1)`{string alternate_name, InodeStore `ENCODE_START(6,4)`{`inode_t` `ENCODE_START(20,6)`, symlink target (if S_ISLNK), dirfragtree, xattr map (user and ACL xattrs live here, not as RADOS xattrs), snap_blob (`sr_t` (8,4) if the inode has a snaprealm, else empty), old_inodes, oldest_snap, damage_flags}}. `inode_t` is encoded with the MDSMap up features and holds, in order, ino, rdev, ctime, mode, uid, gid, nlink, dir_layout, layout, size, truncate fields, mtime, atime, time_warp_seq, client_ranges, dirstat, rstat, accounted_rstat, versions, old_pools, max_size_ever, inline_data, quota, stray_prior_path, scrub stamps, btime, change_attr, export pins, flags, fscrypt fields and optmetadata (CHARMAP=1, QUARANTINE=2; unknown kinds kept opaque). Legacy `'I'` (bare InodeStore) is read only by the MDS but still written by cephfs-data-scan and cephfs-meta-injection. Any other marker throws `malformed_input` and only that dentry is marked damaged.
gates: MDSMap incompat features 9 "file layout v2" and 10 "snaprealm v2"
features.notes: Observations from the map (rados-object-catalog section 8): `damage_flags` is not copied into CInode on load, so the next commit writes 0; the dirfrag commit omits an empty symlink target while `decode_bare` expects one (empty-target symlinks would decode misaligned; unverified in practice); optmetadata kind 3 hits an off-by-one (undefined behaviour). The subvolume marker is persisted only as `sr_t::SUBVOLUME`. Field semantics: [CInode and inode types](../cpp-map/04-cache/cinode-and-inode-types.md).

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Remote (hard link) dentry value
features.summary: Additional names of a hard-linked inode store only the inode number and type.
features.description: Value = u64 `first` + `'l'` + `ENCODE_START(2,1)`{u64 ino, u8 d_type, string alternate_name}; legacy `'L'` (u64 ino, u8 d_type) is read only. A hard-linked inode lives in exactly one primary dentry (possibly in a stray dir); other names carry only ino and d_type and are resolved through `open_ino` (backtraces) when the inode is not cached.
features.notes: cephfs-journal-tool `recover_dentries` writes `'l'` values (src/tools/cephfs/JournalTool.cc:1049).

legacy_parts.note: Reading the unversioned 'L' remote-dentry value (u64 ino, u8 d_type). 'L' values were written by C++ MDS releases up to 15.x, and 16.2.0 introduced the versioned 'l' form with alternate_name. At this commit the MDS and cephfs-journal-tool write 'l', and a grep of src/mds and src/tools finds 'L' only in decoders.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Dirfrag fetch from RADOS
features.summary: Loading a directory fragment into the cache from its omap object.
features.description: `CDir::_omap_fetch` issues one compound read: `OMAP_GETHEADER` + `OMAP_GETVALS` from the start (`mds_dir_keys_per_op` = 16384 requested, but the OSD returns at most 1024 entries or 1 GiB per reply with a `more` flag) plus, on `frag_t()` with `mds_verify_backtrace` > 0, `GETXATTR parent` flagged FAILOK; continuation reads follow, and the whole fetch restarts if a commit completed meanwhile. With `mds_dir_prefetch` = false a keyed `OMAP_GETVALSBYKEYS` for `name_head` keys is used (absent keys become null dentries), optionally followed by a throttled background full fetch. Unlinked directories under a stray without a snaprealm are marked complete and empty without I/O. Only 0, `-ENOENT` or `-ENODATA` are accepted (other read errors assert); a missing or corrupt header becomes a damage entry with `-EIO` to waiters, and the rank goes damaged for the root and its own stray dirs.
features.notes: A duplicate primary inode logs "loaded dup inode" and is not linked unless `mds_hack_allow_loading_invalid_metadata`. On a fetch with `committed_version == 0` a dirty cached item whose on-disk copy has the same ino and version is marked clean. Large dirfrags need many non-atomic round trips. Damage-table policy is owned by 09-background-services ([scrub and damage](../cpp-map/11-background-services/scrub-and-damage.md)); cache side by 05 ([CDir/CDentry](../cpp-map/04-cache/cdir-cdentry-and-cache-objects.md)). One full fetch is in flight per dirfrag (STATE_FETCHING, WAIT_COMPLETE waiters); a full fetch marks the frag complete. fetch_keys reads named keys only and wakes per-name waiters (named lookups when mds_dir_prefetch = false, rejoin prefetch, batched open_ino); fetch_keys with no keys reads only the header of a version-0 dir. Cached entries win over loaded ones and the in-cache fnode wins unless the dir is fresh. A whole dirfrag is processed in one mds_lock critical section with heartbeat resets every mds_heartbeat_reset_grace (1000) items. Code-reading findings (runtime unverified): go_bad does not wake keyed-fetch dentry waiters; a background fetch that hits go_bad never releases its slot, which stops background prefetch for the rank life. See also F-BG-053 (damage on load).

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Dirfrag commit to RADOS
features.summary: Writing dirty dentries and the fnode of a directory fragment back to its omap object.
features.description: `CDir::_commit` captures the dirty dentries under mds_lock; `C_IO_Dir_Commit_Ops` encodes and submits on the rank finisher without mds_lock. Each op chunk of at most `max_dir_commit_size` is [`STAT` guard unless the dirfrag is new] + `OMAP_SETVALS` + `OMAP_RMKEYS` (stale and removed keys first), and `OMAP_SETHEADER(fnode)` is put only in the last chunk, relying on per-object op ordering so that a crash between chunks leaves the old header version. Only dirty dentries are written (a new, fragmenting frag is written in full); a value larger than the limit gets an op of its own. The `STAT` guard makes a vanished object fail with `-ENOENT` instead of being partially recreated; `-ENOENT` is accepted only for a never-committed dirfrag under a stray dir. One commit per dirfrag is in flight; completion advances `committed_version` and cleans items up to it.
features.notes: Other errors go to `handle_write_error` (read-only by default). The fnode header is encoded from the live `CDir::fnode` pointer off-lock while the dentry set was captured earlier, so the header written could be newer than the dentries of that commit (observation; unverified). Op priority comes from segment expiry. commit(want) registers a waiter (the first one auth-pins the dir); _omap_commit snapshots dirty dentries under mds_lock into dentry_commit_item sets (immutable inode/xattr pointers) and removals (null dentries); _committed marks dentries and primary inodes clean up to committed_version, removes clean unreferenced null dentries in stray dirs and restarts a commit for later waiters. See also F-CACHE-016 (when commits happen), F-CACHE-018 (commit errors).

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Base inode objects (.inode)
features.summary: Root and per-rank mdsdir inodes, which have no parent dentry, are stored in objects of their own.
features.description: Root (`1`, stored only by rank 0) and each rank's mdsdir (`0x100+r`) are written with `write_full` of string magic `"ceph fs volume v011"` + InodeStore (6,4) (snap_blob = the `sr_t`) to `<ino>.00000000.inode`: at mkfs, lazily when a base inode is dirty in an expiring segment, and by `CInode::flush`. Fetch reads the `.inode` object and, in parallel, the legacy `inode` xattr on `<ino>.00000000`; a non-empty `.inode` wins; both empty gives `-ENOENT`, wrong magic or a decode error `-EINVAL`, and either at boot marks the rank damaged. Both base inodes always have a snaprealm.
features.notes: Other ranks obtain the root by discover (src/mds/MDCache.cc:685). cephfs-data-scan (`init`, `check_roots`) and cephfs-journal-tool `recover_dentries` read and write these objects.

legacy_parts.note: The parallel read of the legacy 'inode' xattr on <ino>.00000000 and its use when the .inode object is empty. Base inodes were stored in that xattr only by C++ releases before v0.23 (commit 69f5ccdd087, 2010, 'store dir inode in separate object; fetch from both'). CInode::store at this commit writes only <ino>.00000000.inode, and no code in src/mds or src/tools writes the xattr.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Per-rank mdsdir and stray directories
features.summary: On-disk objects of the per-rank mdsdir and its stray directories.
features.description: See F-BG-001. Storage-side facts: mdsdir 0x100+r (S_IFDIR|0500, never fragmented, no backtrace) is stored as `<100+r>.00000000.inode` plus its dirfrag holding the ten primary dentries stray0 .. stray9; each stray dir 0x600+10r+i (S_IFDIR|0500) has its own dirfrags carrying backtrace ancestors [(0x100+r, "stray<i>")] in the metadata pool. Stray dirs are fragmentable (pre-split or merged when the stray index rotates, F-BG-003); directories inside strays are not. populate_mydir at every boot recreates an unreadable mdsdir frag and missing stray dentries (journaled EUpdate; unlike mkfs no backtrace is written) and header-fetches every stray dirfrag to count strays.
features.notes: Old file systems may have the legacy dentry name "stray" (key stray_head) for index 0. Damage to this rank's mdsdir or stray dentries is fatal for the rank (F-BG-057).

legacy_parts.note: Accepting the legacy dentry name "stray" (key stray_head) for stray index 0, named in the notes. The fallback serves file systems created before stray directories were numbered (commit fc212548aea, 2010, first tag v0.24). create_mydir_hierarchy at this commit always creates stray0..stray9.

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Object creation for a new rank (mkfs)
features.summary: Storage view of the objects a new rank writes in up:creating.
features.description: See F-CLU-064.
