Storage-side summary: in one gather the rank writes the journal header and pointer, on rank 0 the root inode `.inode`, dirfrag `1.00000000` and backtrace xattrs, the ten stray dirfrags with backtraces, the mdsdir dirfrag and `.inode`, then `mds<r>_inotable`, an empty `mds<r>_sessionmap`, the PurgeQueue header and, on the tableserver rank, `mds_snaptable`. A previously stopped rank is `up:starting` and reuses its objects.
features.notes: The monitor requires an empty metadata pool for `fs new` unless `--force` (src/mon/FSCommands.cc:211-218).

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Boot-time object loading
features.summary: Storage view of the objects an existing rank reads at boot and how read errors are handled.
features.description: See F-CLU-063 for the boot stages. Storage-side facts: replay reads only journal objects; later phases fetch dirfrags of inodes left undefined, stray dirfrag headers, OpenFileTable prefetch targets and backtraces, probe data objects for size recovery and restart truncates and delegated-ino purges. Read or decode errors of tables, sessionmap, pointer or header mark the rank damaged; -EBLOCKLISTED respawns; OpenFileTable errors only drop prefetch hints.
features.notes: QA expects DAMAGED_ON_START for every deleted metadata object except the journal pointer, the purge queue header, a non-system dirfrag and `mds0_openfiles.0` (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_damage.py:140-152).

features.group: Metadata pool objects: dirfrags, inodes, system tree
features.name: Legacy on-disk formats still decoded
features.summary: Older encodings the C++ MDS still reads, some of which tools still write.
features.description: The C++ MDS still decodes `'I'`/`'L'` dentry values, base inodes stored in the `inode` xattr, the legacy SessionMap data blob (converted with `TRUNCATE 0` plus a full omap rewrite on the next save), the 13-byte OpenFileTable header, journal stream format 0 (rewritten), PurgeItem v1 including the 13.2.2 mis-ordered encoding, a `stray` dentry for index 0, byte-swapped `frag_t` values and `EVENT_SESSIONS_OLD`. cephfs-data-scan (`inject_linkage`) and cephfs-meta-injection still write `'I'` dentries.
features.notes: The legacy SessionMap path aborts on a read error (`ceph_abort_msg`) and has no decode `try` (src/mds/SessionMap.cc:387).

legacy_parts.note: All listed formats except 'I': 'L' remote dentries, base inodes in the 'inode' xattr, the legacy SessionMap data blob and its TRUNCATE-and-rewrite conversion, the 13-byte OpenFileTable header, journal stream format 0 and its rewrite, PurgeItem v1 including the 13.2.2 encoding, the 'stray' dentry for index 0, byte-swapped frag_t values and EVENT_SESSIONS_OLD. Each listed legacy format is written only by older C++ releases: 'L' up to 15.x, the inode xattr before v0.23, the SessionMap blob before v9.0.0, the 13-byte OpenFileTable header by 13.2.0, journal format 0 before v0.82, PurgeItem v1 up to 13.2.2, 'stray' before v0.24, byte-swapped frag_t on big-endian hosts before the 19.2.7/20.2.1/21.0.0 fix, and EVENT_SESSIONS_OLD before v0.58. The 'I' marker is current because cephfs-data-scan (MetadataDriver::inject_linkage) and cephfs-meta-injection at this commit still write it.

features.name: Backtrace parent xattr on object 0
features.summary: Each inode's ancestry is stored on its first object so it can be found by inode number alone.
features.description: `inode_backtrace_t` `ENCODE_START(5,4)`{u64 ino, vector<`inode_backpointer_t` (2,2){dirino, dname, version}> ancestors (parent first, up to the root; the root has none), i64 pool, vector<i64> old_pools} is stored as xattr `parent` on `<ino>.00000000`: the `frag_t()` dirfrag object in the metadata pool for directories, data object 0 in `inode.layout.pool_id` for files, symlinks and special files, always in the pool's default namespace even when `layout.pool_ns` is set. It is written at segment expiry for inodes on `dirty_parent_inodes` (create, mkdir, mknod, symlink, rename including stray moves, unlink to stray, layout change, scrub repair, subtree import, replay) as one compound op `CREATE` (non-exclusive) + `SETXATTR parent` + `SETXATTR layout` [+ `symlink`], batched per pool by `BatchCommitBacktrace` on the finisher without mds_lock. `-ENOENT` counts as success when the inode's current backtrace pool no longer exists; other errors go to `handle_write_error`.
features.notes: Readers: MDS `open_ino`, scrub, cephfs-data-scan `scan_inodes`/`scan_frags` (rebuild dentries from parent, layout and symlink), cephfs-meta-injection. Clients never read backtraces but NFS handles depend on them through LOOKUPINO. A plain link does not rewrite the backtrace; a hard-linked inode's backtrace describes only its primary dentry. `BatchStoredBacktrace` passes the gather's first error to every inode of that pool's batch.

features.name: Layout and symlink xattrs on object 0
features.summary: Object 0 also records the file layout and symlink target for offline recovery tools.
features.description: The backtrace op also sets `layout` (`file_layout_t` encoded with MDSMap up features) on the current pool's object 0 for every inode (directories without `ceph.dir.layout` carry the empty layout, pool -1) and `symlink` (the target string) for symlink inodes when `mds_symlink_recovery` is true. Old-pool copies get only `parent`. cephfs-data-scan reads `layout` and `symlink` (via `cls_cephfs_client`) to rebuild inodes from data objects.

features.name: Backtrace copies in the default data pool and old pools
features.summary: Files outside the default data pool also get a backtrace in it, so lookups can start there.
features.description: `openc` and `mknod` of a file whose layout pool differs from the default (first) data pool add the default pool to `old_pools` and mark the backtrace pool-dirty; every layout change adds the previous pool. With `STATE_DIRTYPOOL` the backtrace is also written (`CREATE` + `SETXATTR parent` only) to object 0 in every old pool, with `pool` naming the current pool. Hence nearly every file has a backtrace object in the default data pool whose `pool` field redirects `open_ino` to the real pool; this is why the monitor requires `--force` for an erasure-coded default data pool.
features.notes: After a rename only the current pool's backtrace is rewritten unless the pool changed, so default-pool copies can carry stale ancestors (their pool field still redirects). An `-ENOENT` from an old-pool copy when the current pool exists goes to `handle_write_error` (read-only by default), and because results are shared per pool batch every inode in that batch sees it (observation, rados-object-catalog section 8).

features.name: Directory backtrace verification on fetch
features.summary: Optional check that a directory's stored backtrace matches its place in the cache.
features.description: With `mds_verify_backtrace` = 1 (default) the frag-0 fetch also reads `parent`; `CInode::verify_diri_backtrace` (skipped for base, dirty-parent and non-auth inodes) compares `ancestors[0]` (dirino, dname) with the cached parent and, on mismatch or a missing xattr, logs "bad backtrace on directory inode", re-dirties the backtrace and flushes the log. Values above 1 assert on mismatch; 0 disables the check.
features.notes: The `parent` value is decoded without `try`, so an undecodable directory backtrace throws out of the fetch completion (observation, src/mds/CInode.cc:1624). The check runs for frag * of an auth, non-base directory without a pending backtrace write; a mismatch logs a cluster-log error and calls mark_dirty_parent, so the backtrace is rewritten at segment expiry; no damage-table entry is created.

features.name: Lookup by inode number through backtraces (open_ino storage path)
features.summary: Backtrace reads that open_ino uses to find an uncached inode by number.
features.description: See F-CACHE-047. Storage-side facts: the backtrace is read with `GETXATTR parent` on object 0 in the hinted pool or the first data pool, re-read in `bt.pool` if the backtrace names another pool, and retried in the metadata pool on `-ENOENT`; a decode error gives `-EIO`, absence in the metadata pool or empty ancestors `-ESTALE`, the same parent twice `-EINVAL`. Kernel NFS re-export handles carry only the 64-bit number (no generation), and libcephfs `ceph_ll_lookup_inode`/`ceph_ll_lookup_vino` do the same, so they depend on this path after restarts and cache trimming.
features.notes: Perf counters `openino_backtrace_fetch`, `openino_dir_fetch`. The backtrace format is F-STORE-058; the LOOKUPINO handler is F-NS-026.

features.name: Scrub tag xattr on object 0
features.summary: The scrub_tag xattr that tagged scrubs set on each visited inode's object 0.
features.description: See F-BG-029. Storage-side facts: the xattr is `scrub_tag` = `encode(std::string tag)` on `<ino hex>.00000000` in the inode's backtrace pool (file layout pool for files, metadata pool for directories), set fire-and-forget with an empty SnapContext, creating object 0 if it is missing; scrub also reads `parent` there to compare with the in-memory backtrace. `cephfs-data-scan --filter-tag` skips objects carrying the tag through the OSD-side `cls_cephfs` PGLS filter `cephfs.inode_tag` (only names ending `.00000000` whose tag differs) or through a client-side getxattr on old OSDs.
features.notes: Counter `scrub_set_tag`. Scrub itself is owned by 09-background-services ([scrub and damage](../cpp-map/11-background-services/scrub-and-damage.md)).

legacy_parts.note: cephfs-data-scan's 'legacy_filtering' path: a client-side getxattr of scrub_tag on every object 0 when the cephfs.inode_tag PGLS filter probe fails. The code comment attributes the fallback to older OSDs without the cephfs PGLS filter mode. The filter exists since 2015 (commit 786d111a972, first tag v10.0.2), and OSDs at this commit load the cephfs object class by default.

features.name: Data object naming and striping shared with clients
features.summary: Clients compute data-object names from inode numbers and layouts, so these are a hard contract.
features.description: Clients read and write file data directly at objects `"%llx.%08llx"` of (ino, object number) in (`layout.pool_id`, `layout.pool_ns`), mapping byte offsets with `Striper::file_to_extents` (stripe_unit, stripe_count, object_size; default 4 MiB, 1, 4 MiB). The inode numbers and layouts the MDS hands out therefore define the data-pool namespace; the MDS uses the same mapping (Filer) for its own data-pool operations and object counts (`Striper::get_num_objects`). Inode numbers must be unique per file system and not reused while objects may exist.
features.notes: Clients may create an empty `<ino>.00000000` in the file's pool and namespace as a pool permission probe (STAT + exclusive CREATE, linux/fs/ceph/addr.c:2487-2506), one reason purge removes object 0 even for empty files. `cephfs-data-scan pg_files` computes the same names. Layout semantics are owned by 04 ([attributes and xattrs](../cpp-map/03-request-path/attributes-and-xattrs.md)).

features.name: Data-object truncation (truncate start/finish and TRIMTRUNC)
features.summary: After a shrinking truncate is journaled, the MDS trims the data objects itself, restartably.
features.description: A shrinking truncate (setattr, open with O_TRUNC) journals `truncate_start` in its EMetaBlob; once safe, clients get `CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC` with the bumped `truncate_seq`, the request is answered, and `MDCache::_truncate_inode` sends `CEPH_OSD_OP_TRIMTRUNC` (object-local truncate offset, truncate_seq, realm SnapContext) to every object overlapping `[truncate_size, truncate_from)`, working backwards with `filer_max_truncate_ops` periods in flight (for fscrypt, first a `WRITE` of the client-supplied last block). Completion journals EUpdate "truncate finish" with `truncate_finish{ino -> start segment seq}`. Segment expiry waits for truncates in progress; replay registers unfinished ones and `recovery_done` restarts them. OSD semantics make this idempotent and safe against racing client I/O: TRIMTRUNC with a seq not newer than the object's is a no-op, client writes with a newer seq truncate first, and older-seq writes are clipped.
features.notes: A single-object truncate asserts the result is 0 or `-ENOENT` (abort otherwise); multi-object per-op errors are ignored. If clients hold buffered snap data the truncate waits for the snapflush. New inodes start with truncate_seq 1 and truncate_size -1, which the OSD treats as "no truncation". Truncate request semantics and CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC are owned by 04 and 03 ([capabilities](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/capabilities.md)). See also F-NS-062 (request), F-CACHE-006 (fields), F-CAPS-016 (TRUNC message), F-CLU-100 (recovery).

features.name: File size and mtime recovery by probing data objects
features.summary: RADOS side of file size and mtime recovery: probing the data objects.
features.description: See F-CAPS-022. Storage-side facts: RecoveryQueue runs a backward Filer::probe from max_size at snapid in->last that issues STAT (RWORDERED) on every object of one period at a time; because mtime is requested it continues down to offset 0. -EBLOCKLISTED respawns; any other probe error marks the whole rank damaged. The I/O context is untracked, so long probes raise no slow-IO warning (F-ADM-077).
features.notes: Counters `recovery_started`, `recovery_completed`, `num_recovering_*` in `mds_cache`.

features.name: Inline data uninlining and the inline_version xattr
features.summary: Scrub moves inline file data into object 0 with an xattr guard shared with clients.
features.description: A scrub visiting a non-directory inode with inline data (internal `CEPH_MDS_OP_UNINLINE_DATA`) issues `CREATE` (non-exclusive, no completion) on `<ino>.00000000` in the layout pool and namespace, then one op `CMPXATTR inline_version GT u64` + `WRITE(0, data, truncate_size, truncate_seq)` + `SETXATTR inline_version = "18446744073709551615"` (`CEPH_INLINE_NONE`). The kernel (`ceph_uninline_data`) and libcephfs use the same op shape with their own decimal inline version, so `inline_version` is a shared guard; a failed guard returns `-ECANCELED` (the kernel treats that as success).
features.notes: The MDS builds the cmpxattr operand with `in->encode(bl, version)`, a full InodeStore encoding, so the OSD compares its first 8 bytes as a u64 (observation, src/mds/MDCache.cc:13548-13556). `C_IO_DataUninlined` completes on a messenger thread and takes mds_lock there. Counters `uninline_started/succeeded/write_failed`. Scrub is owned by 09-background-services. See also F-BG-048 (scrub uninline op), F-CACHE-008 (inline data).

legacy.note: Inodes carry inline data only while the deprecated MDSMap inline_data flag is enabled (accepted only with --yes-i-really-really-mean-it, health FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED, set by no mgr module, cephadm or Rook) or in file systems written by older C++ releases. Scrub uninlining was added in v20.0.0 (commit 8970fef4ecc) to move such data to object 0. The 7.3 kernel's ceph_uninline_data and libcephfs use the same inline_version guard, but only for files that carry inline data.

features.name: MDSTable: versioned single-object table persistence
features.summary: Generic persistence for small tables: one RADOS object rewritten whole, with version counters.
features.description: `InoTable` and `MDSTableServer` derive from `MDSTable`: an in-memory table with `projected_version`, `version` (applied), `committing_version` and `committed_version`, persisted by `write_full` of u64 version + `encode_state()` (applied state only) to `mds<rank>_<name>` (per rank) or `mds_<name>` (global) in the metadata pool, and loaded by `read_full` at CEPH_NOSNAP. `save(onfinish, need)` reuses an in-flight save that covers `need`, otherwise writes the current version and files the waiter under it. Save errors log "failed to store table" and go to `handle_write_error` (waiters never complete); load: `-EBLOCKLISTED` respawns, any other error or decode failure marks the rank damaged.
features.notes: Tables reach RADOS only through segment expiry plus explicit saves at create, after `mds_skip_ino`, after a snap-table format upgrade and after scrub repair; `MDSTable::shutdown` has no caller (mds-tables G7). Each save rewrites the whole object.

legacy_parts.note: The explicit save 'after a snap-table format upgrade' (old-cpp-data) and MDSTable::shutdown, which has no caller (dead-code). upgrade_format changes a table only if its version is 0 or it lacks snaprealm_v2_since (decoded from struct_v < 5, written before v13.1.0), while a table created at this commit starts at version 1 with snaprealm_v2_since set by reset_state. No code calls MDSTable::shutdown.

features.name: InoTable object and per-rank inode ranges
features.summary: The per-rank free list of inode numbers, persisted as one object.
features.description: `mds<r>_inotable` = u64 version + `ENCODE_START(2,2)`{`interval_set<inodeno_t> free`} (u32 count + (start, len) pairs). It is created only in up:creating with free = `[(r+1)<<40, (r+2)<<40)` (2^40 numbers, version 0) and written at segment expiry when `ls->inotablev` exceeds the committed version, after `mds_skip_ino`, and after scrub repair. Two strict interval sets are kept (`projected_free`, `free`): projections happen under mds_lock in request handlers with the event carrying `inotablev = projected_version`, and apply runs from the journal completion, asserting `version == inotablev`. Exhausting the range asserts (`range_start()` on an empty set); there is no ENOSPC path.
features.notes: Tools: `cephfs-table-tool show|reset inode` and `take_inos`, `cephfs-journal-tool event recover_dentries` (`consume_inos`), `cephfs-data-scan scan_links` (`force_consume_to`, which does not check the rank range). A rank consumes its range monotonically except for never-used preallocated numbers.

features.name: Inode number allocation in create paths
features.summary: How openc, mknod, mkdir and symlink obtain a new inode number and journal the allocation.
features.description: `prepare_new_inode(useino = head.ino)`: with an open session it first tries `Session::take_ino` (the useino if it is in the session's durable `prealloc_inos`, else the lowest free preallocated number); otherwise `InoTable::project_alloc_id(useino)` (exactly that number, or the lowest free one). Numbers present in `replay_taken_inos` are skipped. If the result differs from a non-zero useino the cluster log says "<client> specified ino X but mds.N allocated Y". `journal_allocated_inos` records `allocated_ino`, `used_preallocated_ino`, `preallocated_inos`, `client_name`, `inotablev` and `sessionmapv` in the EMetaBlob; `apply_allocated_inos` runs at the safe reply, and the completed-request record stores the created number. Replay applies only missing versions and records skipped allocations as taken.
features.notes: Client-chosen numbers are trusted: a `head.ino` neither in the session preallocation nor free on this rank hits a strict-erase assert; by code reading a kernel async create forwarded to another rank reaches it (mds-tables G2). A stale `alloc_ino` after a taken-number retry can assert (G5). An allocation from the InoTable (not from preallocation) suppresses the early reply. libcephfs sets head.ino on replays of requests that got an unsafe reply (src/client/Client.cc:2852-2855). See also F-NS-041 (client-chosen head.ino), F-NS-040, F-CAPS-053.

features.name: Session inode preallocation and refill
features.summary: Each client session holds a batch of preallocated inode numbers so most creates do not touch the InoTable.
features.description: When a session's free + pending preallocated numbers drop below `mds_client_prealloc_inos / 2`, `prepare_new_inode` projects a batch from the InoTable (`project_alloc_ids`, one version bump) to bring it back to `mds_client_prealloc_inos`; the batch is journaled as `preallocated_inos` and becomes the session's `info.prealloc_inos`, which is the only persisted form (SessionMap); on load `free_prealloc_inos = prealloc_inos`. A session re-opened by force-open while closing may neither use nor refill its preallocation.
features.notes: With preallocation the InoTable is touched only about every 500 creates per session and at session close. Delegating part of the preallocation to clients for async create is owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking ([async dirops](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops.md)). The session also keeps delegated_inos (memory only), which do not count toward the refill threshold. See also F-CAPS-053 (delegation view), F-NS-040 (request view).

features.name: Release of preallocated and delegated numbers at session close (EPurged)
features.summary: Unused inode numbers of a closed session go back to the InoTable; delegated ones only after their object 0 is deleted.
features.description: `journal_close_session` projects the release of the pending and free preallocated numbers and journals `ESession(close, inos_to_free, inotablev, inos_to_purge = delegated_inos)`; on safe `_session_logged` applies the release (asserting the version) and, when the rank is clientreplay/active/stopping, purges the delegated numbers. `MDCache::purge_inodes` `DELETE`s object 0 of each number using the default file layout (first data pool, default namespace, null SnapContext), asserts 0 or `-ENOENT`, then journals `EPurged` (type 24, (1,1): inos, inotablev, seq of the segment that queued the purge) and releases the numbers to the InoTable. Purges recorded while recovering restart from `recovery_done`; segment expiry waits for them (`purging_inodes`).
features.notes: FIXME in code ("handle non-default data pool and namespace"): objects an async-create client wrote into a non-default pool or namespace are not removed, and the numbers are then handed out again, so a later file can find a stale object under its name (mds-tables G23, code reading). A session that fails to reconnect has its delegated and free preallocated sets swapped first, so its unused preallocation is purged before release. `mds_wipe_ino_prealloc` (dev) clears the sets without returning them. Delegation itself is owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. This path does not use strays or the PurgeQueue; ESession replay re-adds the numbers to the segment's purging_inodes. Up to 500 deletes per session close with default options (the delegation target, F-CAPS-054). Because the C++ MDS never grants Dc/Dr (lock-cache finding in F-CAPS-054), no unmodified client performs async creates, so these deletes target numbers no client used and most return -ENOENT. EPurged::print spells the event name "Eurged". See also F-CLU-101 (start after recovery), F-CAPS-054 (delegation), F-PROTO-049 (session close).

features.name: Inode numbers are never reused after deletion
features.summary: Deleting a file never returns its inode number to the allocator.
features.description: Purging a deleted inode never returns its number to the InoTable: StrayManager and PurgeQueue make no InoTable calls, and the only releases are never-used preallocated or delegated numbers. A rank therefore consumes its 2^40 range monotonically, and data-object names and NFS file handles (64-bit ino, no generation number) never alias a newer file, except for delegated numbers released after a partial purge (F-STORE-072).
features.notes: With the kernel `ino32` mount option numbers are folded to low32 ^ high32, so distinct 64-bit numbers can collide in what user space sees (linux/fs/ceph/super.h:579-628).

features.name: InoTable replay, gap repair and the taken-number guard
features.summary: How replay brings the InoTable up to the journal and protects against numbers it wrongly believes free.
features.description: EMetaBlob replay calls `replay_alloc_id`/`replay_alloc_ids` only if the loaded table version is below `inotablev` (each bumps the version by one; numbers not in `free` are logged); a remaining gap is logged ("journal replay inotablev mismatch"), force-set and then asserted equal. ESession and EPurged replay `replay_release_ids` with an exact-version assert and no repair. `MDCache::replay_taken_inos` collects numbers of replayed events whose table update was already reflected or skipped, and every inode loaded from a dirfrag; `prepare_new_inode` skips such numbers (tracker 52280); entries leave the set when the inode leaves the cache.
features.notes: `repair()`, `skip_inos()` and the taken-number apply bump the version without a journal event; if the following save is lost, a session close or purge as the first InoTable event aborts replay (mds-tables G3, code reading). `replay_taken_inos` is a plain std::set with one entry per inode loaded from disk that is still cached. See also F-BG-042 (scrub InoTable repair).

features.name: SessionMap object
features.summary: Per-rank omap object persisting client sessions, their preallocated numbers and completed request ids.
features.description: `mds<r>_sessionmap`: omap header `ENCODE_START(1,1)`{u64 version}; key = printed entity name (`client.<id>`) -> `session_info_t` `ENCODE_START(7,7)`{entity_inst_t, completed_requests map<tid, created ino>, prealloc_inos, u32 0 (legacy used_inos), completed_flushes, auth_name, client_metadata_t (3,1){kv map, feature bitset, metric_spec}}. `SessionMap::save` (at expiry when `sessionmapv` exceeds committed, or early when the dirty set reaches `mds_sessionmap_keys_per_op`) writes header + dirty open/closing/stale/killing sessions + `OMAP_RMKEYS` of null sessions in one op; `save_if_dirty` writes only sessions whose completed_requests changed, in batches of `mds_sessionmap_keys_per_op`, without touching the header. Load pages with `OMAP_GETVALS`; all loaded sessions start OPEN (they go stale or are evicted if they do not reconnect); any read or decode error marks the rank damaged.
features.notes: `cephfs-table-tool reset session` = `omap_clear` (FAILOK) + fresh header. Persisted completed_requests let a recovered rank answer retried requests idempotently; persisted auth_name and client_metadata allow Ganesha reclaim after failover. The session state machine is owned by 02-client-sessions-and-protocol ([sessions](../cpp-map/02-client-protocol/sessions.md)).

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: SnapTable object (mds_snaptable)
features.summary: The global snapshot table object, written only by the table server rank.
features.description: `mds_snaptable` (only on the tableserver, always rank 0) = u64 version + SnapServer `ENCODE_START(5,3)`{last_snap, snaps map<snapid, SnapInfo>, need_to_purge map<pool, set<snapid>>, pending_update, pending_destroy, pending_noop, last_created, last_destroyed, snaprealm_v2_since}, followed outside that envelope by `pending_for_mds` map<version, `mds_table_pending_t` (2,2){reqid, mds, tid}>. A fresh table starts `last_snap` at max(1, highest `snap_seq` of the data pools in the OSDMap) and version 1. It is written at mkfs, at segment expiry when `tablev` exceeds the committed version (every expiry pass that needs it issues a full `write_full`, even if one is in flight), and after a format upgrade at replay_done. Because `pending_for_mds` is saved, a prepared but unresolved transaction survives trimming of its PREPARE event.
features.notes: first-damage.py reads raw bytes: byte 8 must be struct_v 5 and bytes 14-21 are `last_snap` (src/tools/cephfs/first-damage.py:158-167). `cephfs-table-tool reset snap` writes version 1 with `last_snap = 1` because it consults no OSDMap. `cephfs-data-scan scan_links` uses `SnapServer::force_update`. Snapshot semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes ([snapshots](../cpp-map/10-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes/snapshots.md)). See also F-SNAP-001 (snap id allocation).

legacy_parts.note: The write 'after a format upgrade at replay_done' (SnapServer::upgrade_format) and the struct_v < 5 decode default that triggers it. Only tables written before v13.1.0 (no snaprealm_v2_since, commit aedd5301dcb) or with version 0 are upgraded. reset_state at this commit sets snaprealm_v2_since = last_snap + 1 and MDSTableServer::reset_state raises the version to 1, so tables created now never trigger the upgrade.

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: Table server/client two-phase commit and its journal events
features.summary: MDS-to-MDS protocol that applies changes to the global snap table atomically with the requesting rank's update.
features.description: `MMDSTableRequest` (`MSG_MDS_TABLE_REQUEST` 102: u16 table, s16 op whose sign gives the direction, u64 reqid, bufferlist; tid in the message header) carries: PREPARE -> the server journals `ETableServer` PREPARE (flushed; tid = the new server version) -> AGREE -> the client journals its decision as `EMetaBlob.table_tids` inside its own EUpdate -> COMMIT -> the server journals ETableServer COMMIT -> ACK -> the client journals `ETableClient` ACK. `ETableServer` (type 43, (3,3): stamp, table, op PREPARE 3/COMMIT 5/ROLLBACK 7/SERVER_UPDATE 8, reqid, bymds, mutation, tid, version) sets the segment's `tablev` (expiry saves the table); `table_tids` put the tid in `pending_commit_tids`, and expiry waits until the ACK is logged; `ETableClient` (type 42, (3,3): stamp, table, op ACK = -6, tid). The requester replies to its client after its own EUpdate is safe, without waiting for the ACK. The only table is the snap table (`TABLE_SNAP` = 1); `TABLE_ANCHOR` = 0 has no implementation and its old events are skipped.
features.notes: Only PREPARE is flushed explicitly; COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SERVER_UPDATE and ACK become durable at the next flush (tick, object boundary, expiry). Server-side asserts (duplicate ROLLBACK, COMMIT with tid > version, SERVER_UPDATE received as a message) and leaked prepares when a request dies are listed as mds-tables G8 and G10. A message for TABLE_ANCHOR would dereference a NULL server/client. Snapshot requests (mksnap, rmsnap, renamesnap, snap metadata) are owned by 08. See also F-SNAP-002 (SnapServer and SnapClient).

legacy_parts.note: Skipping TABLE_ANCHOR (table 0) records during replay ('its old events are skipped'): get_table_server and get_table_client return NULL, and ETableServer, ETableClient and EMetaBlob table_tids replay ignore them. Anchor-table records exist only in journals written by C++ releases before v0.81 (anchor table removed by commit 913a5dd4eab, 2013). Ranks at this commit journal only TABLE_SNAP transactions.

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: Table server placement on rank 0
features.summary: The global table server always runs on rank 0, making snapshot operations depend on it.
features.description: `MDSMap::tableserver` is initialised to 0, never assigned and encoded in every MDSMap; rank 0 loads or creates `mds_snaptable`, writes ETableServer events and runs `SnapServer`, while every rank (including 0) runs a `SnapClient`. All snapshot creation, removal, renaming and metadata updates, the expiry of any rank's segments holding un-acked snap commits, survivors' resolve answers and leaving up:reconnect depend on rank 0 being up.
features.notes: The kernel decodes and discards `tableserver` (linux/fs/ceph/mdsmap.c:310-313); `ceph fs dump` prints it.

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: NOTIFY_PREP fan-out barrier
features.summary: Before a snap table change is agreed, every active rank receives the full table and must acknowledge it.
features.description: After a prepare is logged, `SnapServer::_notify_prep` sends `NOTIFY_PREP(tid)` with a full copy of the snap table (snaps, pending_update, pending_destroy, last_created, last_destroyed) to every rank in `active_clients` (ranks >= up:resolve, including the requester and rank 0) and parks the AGREE until every rank answered `NOTIFY_ACK` or failed. Because NOTIFY_PREP reaches the requester before the AGREE on the same connection, its cache already covers the tid when the request resumes (asserted). There is no timeout: an active rank that never acks blocks the AGREE indefinitely.
features.notes: Cost grows with the number of snapshots times the number of ranks (mds-tables G22).

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: Server-local table updates and table queries
features.summary: Server-only journaled updates (purged snap ids) and the query protocol that keeps client caches in sync.
features.description: `do_server_update` journals `ETableServer` SERVER_UPDATE (no client, not flushed) and applies it on safe; the snap table uses it to drop purged snapids from `need_to_purge` after the OSDMap or the monitor's `MRemoveSnaps` reply shows them removed. `QUERY`/`QUERY_REPLY` refresh a client rank's cached copy (`'U'` up to date, or `'F'` plus the full state, server version in the header tid); `SnapClient::sync` marks the cache synced when a reply with reqid >= `sync_reqid` arrives; resolve answers of survivors and leaving up:reconnect wait for a synced cache.
features.notes: `TABLESERVER_OP_SERVER_UPDATE` (8) is never sent on the wire; receiving it would hit `ceph_abort_msg`. MRemoveSnaps and snap id allocation are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes.

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: Table 2PC recovery and message delivery rules
features.summary: How prepared snap-table transactions are completed or rolled back when rank 0 or a client rank fails.
features.description: Persistent state is the table object (with `pending_for_mds`) plus rank 0's journal, and on clients the journaled `table_tids` minus logged ACKs. When rank 0 recovers, `finish_recovery` re-sends NOTIFY_PREP for pending transactions, then AGREE for every pending tid of an active requester, then `SERVER_READY` (next reqid); clients resend queries, prepares and commits. When a client rank recovers, rank 0 re-sends its AGREEs; a tid the client never journaled is answered with ROLLBACK (presumed abort), journaled ones get COMMIT again, and a COMMIT for an already committed tid is ACKed at once. Parked notifies whose requester failed become rollbacks. Delivery rules relied on: messages to ranks down in the sender's map are dropped, to creating/starting/replay ranks deferred, and the sender pushes its newer MDSMap first; stale messages are dropped; table clients drop messages while below up:resolve unless they want resolve.
features.notes: By code reading a duplicate ROLLBACK can reach rank 0 when a client rank fails twice within one flush interval and abort rank 0 (mds-tables G8). The resolve exchange is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha ([resolve and rejoin](../cpp-map/09-recovery/resolve-and-rejoin.md)). See also F-CLU-078 (effect on other ranks' recovery), F-STORE-083 (resolve integration).

features.group: Table server/client 2PC and the SnapTable object
features.name: Resolve integration of table commits
features.summary: Ranks tell each other, during resolve, which snap table commits they have journaled but not seen acknowledged.
features.description: A recovering rank captures `get_journaled_tids()` at resolve start and puts them into every `MMDSResolve` it sends (`table_clients` {u8 type, set<version_t> pending_commits}); survivors send their current ones. Receivers call `notify_commit(tid)` so every snap cache treats those snapshots as committing; survivors sync their snap cache before sending subtree resolves. `MMDSSnapUpdate` messages carrying a tid also call `notify_commit` on receivers.

features.name: OpenFileTable tracking and Anchor records
features.summary: Each rank keeps a ref-counted set of open inodes, the directories containing them, and all their ancestors.
features.description: Anchors (`ino`, `dirino`, `d_name`, `d_type`, `set<frag_t> frags`; `Anchor` `ENCODE_START(2,1)`) are kept for inodes with "notable" caps (a client cap whose wanted set includes any write, FILE_WR or FILE_RD, or other ranks wanting caps), inodes with client writeable ranges, dirfrags containing an inode with any client cap, and every ancestor of these through whatever inodes are cached (including replicas owned by other ranks). `get_ref`/`put_ref` walk up the parent chain; link/unlink hooks rewrite an anchor's parent; dirty items are DIRTY_NEW, DIRTY_UNDEF or the omap slot of a key to remove. The table is a recovery aid, not a source of truth. The old global anchor table (`TABLE_ANCHOR`, `mds_anchortable`) no longer exists; hard links and LOOKUPINO use backtraces instead.
features.notes: Common ancestors (root, subvolume roots, hot directories) are walked on every first or last open below them. `STATE_TRACKEDBYOFT` is kept across export/import but not across fragmentation, where the cap hooks re-add the new frags.

features.name: OpenFileTable objects and commit with redo journal
features.summary: The open-file set is written to a few omap objects, atomically per object and with a small redo journal across objects.
features.description: `mds<r>_openfiles.<idx hex>` (at most 1024 objects, at most `osd_deep_scrub_large_omap_object_key_threshold` = 200000 keys each, empty data): omap header string magic `"ceph fs volume v011"` + `ENCODE_START(1,1)`{u64 omap_version, u32 omap_num_objs, u8 journal_state 0 NONE/1 START/2 FINISH}; key `"%llx"` ino -> Anchor + u32 0. `commit(log_seq)` runs once per trim pass when anchors are dirty or a newer segment exists (one commit in flight): if at most one object changes and the count is unchanged, one atomic op (header NONE + `omap_set` + `omap_rm_keys`, plus a FAILOK `omap_clear` for a new object); otherwise phase 1 writes `_journal.<n>` keys {omap_version, to_update, to_remove} with header START, and phase 2, after every phase-1 ack, applies them with header FINISH and removes the journal keys. Shrinking only lowers `omap_num_objs`; tail objects are never deleted and are cleared before reuse.
features.notes: No tool or mgr module reads these objects (QA test_openfiletable.py expects `mds0_openfiles.1` with a key limit of 5). A write error leaves the commit "in flight" forever, so no later commit starts and expiry stalls (mds-tables G9). More than 1024 x MAX_ITEMS_PER_OBJ anchors asserts (G13). A rank in up:starting never loads its OFT and its first commit starts from object 0 again (G18).

features.name: OpenFileTable load and redo-journal recovery
features.summary: Loads the open-file hints at boot, completing or discarding an interrupted multi-object commit.
features.description: Loaded asynchronously at boot for up:replay and at standby-replay takeover (never for creating or starting): every object's header and keys up to `omap_num_objs` of the highest-version header are read; `_journal.*` entries of the current version are replayed only when `journal_state` is FINISH (roll forward), otherwise discarded (roll back); then headers are rewritten and journal keys removed. Any read or decode error (including `-ENOENT`) resets the table to empty and the rank continues without prefetch hints.
features.notes: Code-reading corner cases (mds-tables G11, G12): two headers of one generation disagreeing on the object count hit a `ceph_assert` at every boot until the objects are removed; a crash during a shrinking commit can index beyond the per-object counters.

features.name: OpenFileTable-gated segment expiry
features.summary: A journal segment can expire only after the open-file set has been committed past it.
features.description: `LogSegment::try_to_expire` registers `wait_for_commit(seq)` when the log is not capped and `seq >= committed_log_seq`, so segment s expires only after an OFT commit with `log_seq > s`; `trim` and `trim_to` end with `try_to_commit_open_file_table(last segment seq)` at `CEPH_MSG_PRIO_HIGH` when anchors are dirty or a newer segment exists. This is what lets expiry drop head inodes from `open_files` instead of re-journaling them.
features.notes: A slow OFT commit stalls trimming (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 23).

features.name: EOpen suppression (should_log_open)
features.summary: Opens are journaled as EOpen only when the OpenFileTable does not already cover them.
features.description: `OpenFileTable::should_log_open` decides whether an open (`Server::handle_client_open` for auth head inodes) or a cap-wanted change (`Locker::adjust_cap_wanted`) must still journal an EOpen: not needed if the inode is tracked and either `last_journaled >= committing_log_seq` or it is not dirty in the OFT. The EOpen is submitted without waiting for it.

features.name: OpenFileTable prefetch during rejoin
features.summary: A recovering rank opens all inodes recorded as open before it processes client cap reconnects.
features.description: `MDCache::process_imported_caps` runs `prefetch_inodes` (after the load): DIR_INODES opens every directory anchor (metadata pool, with ancestor hints from the loaded anchors so `open_ino` traverses dirfrags instead of reading backtraces first), the optional DIRFRAGS stage fetches recorded dirfrags, and FILE_INODES opens every file anchor (first data pool for the backtrace fallback), skipping numbers destroyed in the replayed journal. Inodes found to be owned by another rank get their reconnected caps exported there.
features.notes: Rejoin is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha ([resolve and rejoin](../cpp-map/09-recovery/resolve-and-rejoin.md)). See also F-CLU-087 (cap matching in rejoin).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: Per-rank Objecter RADOS client
features.summary: One RADOS client per rank, shared by every MDS subsystem.
features.description: Each MDSRank creates one `Objecter` on the daemon's messenger, shared by all subsystems (PurgeQueue wraps it in its own Filer and Journaler on the `mds-pq-fin` finisher; MDCache and RecoveryQueue own Filers on the rank finisher); it subscribes to OSDMaps. The MDS never uses object-class `exec`, watch/notify, `APPEND`, `CMPEXT` or `ROLLBACK`, matching the cephadm OSD cap `allow rw tag cephfs *=*` (no `x`). `objecter_inflight_ops`/`objecter_inflight_op_bytes` (1024 / 100 MiB) are counted but never block the MDS (no `keep_balanced_budget`), so in-flight RADOS work is bounded only by per-subsystem limits.
features.notes: The only `op_cancel` is the Mantle read timeout. cephadm re-applies `mon 'profile mds' osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*' mds 'allow'` on deploy (src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/services/cephadmservice.py:1527). See also F-PROTO-105 (Objecter duties).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: RADOS identity and request ids
features.summary: How OSDs tell the ops of a new MDS instance apart from those of the previous holder of the rank.
features.description: Ops are sent as entity `mds.<rank>` (`mds.<gid>` in standby-replay, `mds.-1` before a rank is held) with client incarnation = `mds_info_t::inc`, which the monitor sets to the FSMap epoch at promotion, and per-process tids starting at 0; the messenger nonce is random per process. OSDs detect duplicate requests by (entity, incarnation, tid) and answer them from the PG log, so the incarnation keeps a new instance's reqids distinct from the old one's. OSDs also special-case MDS senders for full handling.
features.notes: See also F-CLU-038 (rank incarnation).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: FULL_FORCE: MDS I/O ignores full flags
features.summary: Journaling, writeback and purges continue when the cluster or a pool is marked full.
features.description: `objecter->unset_honor_pool_full()` makes the MDS Objecter ignore cluster and pool full flags and add `CEPH_OSD_FLAG_FULL_FORCE` to every op; OSDs additionally exempt MDS senders from full-flag discards and accept writes to `FLAG_FULL` pools from MDS reqids. Ops are still paused by `PAUSERD`/`PAUSEWR` (`ceph osd pause`) and by the Objecter epoch barrier, and the OSD fail-safe check (`osd_failsafe_full_ratio`, 0.97) silently drops write-ordered ops without `FULL_TRY`, including the MDS's, without a reply.
features.notes: With `rados_osd_op_timeout` = 0 (default) dropped writes stay in flight; the symptoms are MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO and stalled journal flushes (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 1).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: Continuous OSDMap following
features.summary: The MDS tracks every OSDMap and applies full, blocklist, purge-limit and snap-removal policy to each.
features.description: After each OSDMap the Objecter re-subscribes ("onetime", renewed each time), making the subscription effectively continuous. `MDSRankDispatcher::handle_osd_map` then runs under mds_lock: snap removal reporting on the tableserver, recomputing `Server::is_full`, updating the PurgeQueue op limit, and, outside (standby-)replay, killing client sessions blocklisted in the map.
features.notes: The blocklist session scan is O(sessions) per OSDMap.

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: wait_for_map and wait_for_latest_osdmap
features.summary: Helpers that wait until the MDS has a given or the latest OSDMap.
features.description: `wait_for_map(E)` completes immediately if the Objecter has epoch >= E; otherwise it asks the monitor for the latest committed osdmap version and waits for that epoch, without re-checking E. `wait_for_latest_osdmap` does the same unconditionally. Callers: `replay_start` and the standby-replay final pass (fencing), client eviction, the `osdmap barrier` admin command and layout vxattr pool lookups. Completions run on the 2-thread asio pool and hop to the rank finisher.
features.notes: Correct for fencing only if the answering monitor's latest version is >= E; Paxos batching makes that hold on the monitor that published the MDSMap, and a lagging monitor is an unverified gap (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 13).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: I/O completion path and self-respawn when fenced
features.summary: RADOS completions re-enter the MDS on one finisher under mds_lock; a blocklisted instance restarts itself.
features.description: OSD replies complete on messenger threads; the MDS wraps completions in `C_OnFinisher` (single `mds-rank-fin` thread) or `C_IO_Wrapper`, and `MDSIOContextBase::complete` takes mds_lock, drops the callback if the daemon is stopping, and respawns on `-EBLOCKLISTED` or `-ETIMEDOUT` before calling `finish(r)`. Respawn is `execv` of the same binary with a new random nonce, which the old address blocklist does not cover; the same rule applies in `handle_write_error`, the journal write handler, pointer/journal recovery and table loads, while journal replay read errors other than `-ENOENT`/`-EINVAL` exit via `suicide()`. Exceptions to the finisher path: PurgeQueue completions on its own finisher, `C_IO_DataUninlined` on a messenger thread, blocking recovery-thread I/O, and dirfrag commit and backtrace batches encoded on the finisher without mds_lock.
gates: rados_osd_op_timeout (default 0; > 0 turns slow ops into -ETIMEDOUT and a respawn)
features.notes: The heartbeat deliberately has no suicide grace: the monitor blocklists a daemon that stops beaconing (src/mds/MDSRank.cc:1369). Every completion serializing on one thread and mds_lock is classified as not inherent by the map (rados-and-osd-interactions section 6). See also F-CLU-105 (respawn).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: OSD epoch barrier in cap messages
features.summary: Clients must have at least the OSDMap that fenced an evicted client before using caps the MDS hands out.
features.description: `MDSRank::osd_epoch_barrier` is included in every `MClientCaps` (field since message v5); clients raise their own barrier and pause OSD requests until they have that OSDMap, and echo their barrier in caps and cap releases (v2+). Sources: eviction (epoch after `wait_for_latest_osdmap`), a blocklist scan that killed sessions, every MDSMap processed while active (current epoch), client-supplied higher barriers (which also set the MDS Objecter's `epoch_barrier`, pausing all MDS RADOS ops until that map arrives), and the admin command `osdmap barrier <epoch>`, which sets it and blocks until the map is present. `status` reports `osdmap_epoch` and `osdmap_epoch_barrier`. Every setter except the client path assigns unconditionally, so the rank barrier can go down.
features.notes: Raising the barrier on every MDSMap while active makes clients fetch newer OSDMaps after unrelated MDSMap changes. QA uses the admin command and status (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_full.py:33, :81). libcephfs implements the same exchange (`cap_epoch_barrier`, src/client/Client.cc:19013). See also F-PROTO-092 (MClientCapRelease barrier), F-ADM-043 (osdmap barrier command).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: Metadata-pool-full ENOSPC policy
features.summary: When the metadata pool is full, metadata operations that would grow it are refused.
features.description: `Server::is_full` = `FLAG_FULL` of the metadata pool in the last OSDMap (data pools and the cluster FULL flag are not consulted). While set, SETLAYOUT, SETDIRLAYOUT, SETXATTR, RMXATTR, CREATE (open with O_CREAT), SYMLINK, MKSNAP and LINK/RENAME before witnesses are refused unless the session's MDS cap grants `f` on the request's base inode; SETATTR growing the size beyond max(size, old_size) gets `-ENOSPC` regardless; unlink, rmdir, mkdir, mknod, open and truncate down proceed and purge keeps freeing space. The intended error is `-ENOSPC`, but `Server::check_access` has already replied `-EACCES`, so clients see `-EACCES` and drop the second (`-ENOSPC`) reply as an unknown tid.
features.notes: The MDS also runs `request_finish` twice for such a request (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 33). Data writes fail with `-ENOSPC` on the client side (kernel ABORT_ON_FULL; libcephfs cancels writes and raises its barrier). The `f` cap is owned by 11-security-admin-and-observability ([auth caps](../cpp-map/01-cluster-integration/auth-and-mds-caps.md)). See also F-NS-018 (position in dispatch), F-ADM-014 (f flag).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: Metadata write-error policy and read-only mode
features.summary: What the MDS does when writing a backing object fails: go read-only (default), respawn, or ignore.
features.description: Errors on backing-object writes (tables, sessionmap, OpenFileTable, backtraces, dirfrags, base inodes, expiry sub-operations, PurgeQueue journal) go to `MDSRank::handle_write_error`: `-EBLOCKLISTED` respawns; otherwise `mds_action_on_write_error` 0 logs and ignores, 1 (default) calls `MDCache::force_readonly` (CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO to all open/stale sessions and to new sessions right after OPEN, write caps revoked, `-EROFS` for write requests, no fragmentation or stray evaluation, trimming stops, health MDS_READ_ONLY), and 2 or more respawns. Several completions instead assert unless the result is 0 or `-ENOENT` (or `-ENODATA`): dirfrag read, data truncation, old-frag purge and delegated-ino purge abort the daemon. Journal write errors always mark the rank damaged.
features.notes: The kernel marks the session read-only on FORCE_RO (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:4647). A read-only PurgeQueue completing `push` inline with `-EROFS` can self-deadlock on mds_lock (rados-and-osd-interactions section 8 item 25, code reading, not reproduced). See also F-CLU-107 (failure exits), F-PROTO-038 (FORCE_RO), F-ADM-042 (force_readonly), F-CACHE-018 (dirfrag commit errors).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: Pool requirements for CephFS pools
features.summary: Constraints the monitor enforces on metadata and data pools, which the MDS relies on.
features.description: The monitor (`_check_pool`, `fs new`, `fs add_data_pool`) requires a non-erasure-coded metadata pool (even an omap-capable EC pool is refused), an empty metadata pool at `fs new` unless `--force`, `--force` for an EC default data pool (every file's backtrace lands there), `allow_ec_overwrites` for other EC data pools, no pool snapshots (and later refuses `osd pool mksnap` and unmanaged snaps on FS pools), no cache tier, and tags pools with application `cephfs` (`data`/`metadata` = fs name); a pool in an FSMap cannot be deleted (`-EBUSY`). The MDS caches the metadata pool id for the rank's lifetime, needs read/write on the metadata and all data pools, and requires layout pools to be in `MDSMap::data_pools`.
gates: MDSMap incompat features 4, 6, 8 "no anchor table", 9, 10, 11, 12 "quiesce subvolumes" describe the on-disk format and gate which daemons may join
features.notes: The `fs new` command and FSMap are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha ([FSMap and MDSMap](../cpp-map/01-cluster-integration/fsmap-and-mdsmap.md)). See also F-CLU-042 (fs new).

features.group: RADOS client, fencing and pool policy
features.name: Metadata pool shared with mgr-owned objects
features.summary: The metadata pool also holds objects written by mgr modules and cephfs-mirror that the MDS never touches.
features.description: mgr `snap_schedule` stores `snap_db_v0` (namespace `cephfs-snap-schedule`, a legacy dump read once and removed) and its libcephsqlite database `snap_db_v0.db`, striped as `<file>.<16 hex digits>` in the default namespace; mgr `mirroring` and the cephfs-mirror daemons use the `cephfs_mirror` object (omap keys `dir_map_*`, `instance_*`, `sync_stat/<fs>/...`, watch/notify). mgr/volumes opens no ioctx. These objects live beside the MDS objects in the metadata pool; the C++ MDS object names (hexadecimal inode-number names and the mds<r>_* table objects) do not collide with them, and the MDS does not create, modify or delete them.
features.notes: The naming of SQLite's rollback-journal objects is unverified in the map. Objects: default namespace snap_db_v0.db.<16 hex> and snap_db_v0.db-journal.<16 hex> (snap_schedule, with striper.* xattrs and striper.lock), cephfs_mirror (mirroring omap and watch/notify), cephfs_mirror.<instance id> (mirror daemon instances); namespace cephfs-snap-schedule: legacy snap_db_v0. Rook clusters: ceph-csi journal objects csi.volumes.default and csi.volume.<id> in namespace csi. Data pools: cephfs-data-scan adds scan_ceiling, scan_max_size, scan_max_mtime and scan_pool_id xattrs on 0th objects (removed by cleanup).

legacy_parts.note: The snap_schedule module's one-time import and removal of the legacy snap_db_v0 dump object in namespace cephfs-snap-schedule. The snap_db_v0 dump object was written by the 16.2.x snap_schedule module, and 17.2.0 and later only read it once, replay it into the libcephsqlite database and remove it. The writer was an older mgr module rather than the C++ MDS, so old-cpp-data is the nearest reason code.

features.group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
features.name: Journal and OpenFileTable perf counters
features.summary: Counters describing journal size, throughput, trimming and replay, plus OpenFileTable size.
features.description: `mds_log` logger: `evadd`, `ev`, `seg`, `replayed` (priority interesting); `evlrg` (events of at least `mds_log_event_large_threshold`), `evexg`, `evexd`, `segexg`, `segexd`, `segmjr`, `jlat` (journal flush latency), `evex`, `evtrm`, `segadd`, `segex`, `segtrm` (useful); `expos`, `wrpos`, `rdpos` (debug, not sent to the mgr). Consumers: `ceph fs status` shows the `mds_log.replayed` rate as standby-replay "Evts/s"; the dashboard requests `mds_log.ev` (and a non-existent `mds_log.replay`); the Grafana mixin uses `ceph_mds_log_evadd`, `ceph_mds_log_ev`, `ceph_mds_log_seg`. The `oft` logger (`omap_total_objs`, `omap_total_kv_pairs`, `omap_total_updates`, `omap_total_removes`) has priority 0, is not sent to the mgr, and is updated only on slow-path commits.
gates: mgr_stats_threshold (5) decides which counters reach the mgr
features.notes: Per-subsystem storage counters elsewhere: `mds.dir_fetch_*`, `dir_commit`, `openino_*`, `scrub_*`, `mds_sessions.mdthresh_evicted`, `purge_queue.*` (rados-object-catalog section 5.3). See also F-ADM-066 (perf counter loggers).

features.group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
features.name: Op tracker journal events
features.summary: Per-request trace points for journal submission and commit in the op tracker.
features.description: Requests record the op-tracker event `submit entry: <fn>` at submission and `journal_committed: ` when the log completion runs (`ServerLogContext::pre_finish`, before mds_lock is taken), visible in `dump_ops_in_flight` and the historic ops dumps.
features.notes: See also F-ADM-035 (op tracker dumps).

features.group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
features.name: Offline journal reset and EResetJournal
features.summary: Disaster-recovery reset of a rank's journal, and the event that tells the MDS a reset happened.
features.description: `cephfs-journal-tool --rank=<fs>:<rank> journal reset [--force] --yes-i-really-really-mean-it`: a soft reset recovers the front journal, moves read/write/expire to `round_up(old_end + 1, period)`, writes the header (whose commit trims the old objects) and appends `EResetJournal`; `--force` rewrites the pointer to `{0x200+rank, 0}`, creates a fresh journal with the default layout and `mds_journal_format`, and appends EResetJournal. `EResetJournal` (type 9, (2,2), stamp only, no seq, so its segment seq becomes its byte offset) is a major boundary whose replay wipes the session map, skips 10,000,000 inode numbers in the InoTable (two version bumps), and claims the root (on the rank owning root) and mydir subtrees. Related dev options applied at replay_done: `mds_skip_ino` (skip N numbers and save the table), `mds_wipe_ino_prealloc`, `mds_wipe_sessions`.
features.notes: The tool's only liveness check refuses with `-EPERM` when the rank is up:active in the MDSMap; replay, clientreplay, stopping and other states pass (src/tools/cephfs/JournalTool.cc:146-151). A hard reset leaves the previous journal inode's objects in place. Documented in doc/cephfs/disaster-recovery-experts.rst.

features.group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
features.name: cephfs-journal-tool inspection, export/import, header and event commands
features.summary: The offline tool that reads, edits and splices the journal and recovers dentries from it.
features.description: Besides reset, cephfs-journal-tool (JournalScanner, JournalTool, Dumper) reads the pointer (or `<0x500+rank>` with `--journal=purge_queue`), header and objects and finds corrupt ranges by sentinel search; offers `journal inspect/export/import` (import purges or zeroes trailing objects), `header get/set` (trimmed_pos, expire_pos, write_pos, pool_id) and `header recover` (finds the first SUBTREEMAP/SUBTREEMAP_TEST/LID/RESETJOURNAL), and `event get|splice|recover_dentries`. Events are decoded with `LogEvent::decode_event`; `splice` overwrites ranges with `ENoOp` (type 51, (2,2): u32 pad_size + pad_size bytes of 0xff, decode requires exactly that many bytes, replay no-op, encoded with `CEPH_FEATURES_SUPPORTED_DEFAULT`); `recover_dentries` writes fullbits back as `'i'`/`'l'` dentries, fnode headers and base `.inode` objects and consumes the inode numbers in `mds<r>_inotable`. It is the only offline tool that decodes MDS events; cephfs-data-scan never reads the journal.

features.group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
features.name: Other offline tools over the on-disk format
features.summary: Repair and inspection tools that parse or write the C++ MDS object formats directly.
features.description: `cephfs-table-tool` (show/reset of session, snap and inode tables; `take_inos`); `cephfs-data-scan` (scan_extents, scan_inodes, scan_frags, scan_links, init, cleanup, pg_files: reads object-0 xattrs `parent`, `layout`, `symlink`, `scrub_tag` in the default namespace, writes `'I'` dentries, blank fnodes, root and mdsdir `.inode`, `lost+found`, InoTable `force_consume_to`, `SnapServer::force_update`, `scan_*` xattrs via `cls_cephfs`); `first-damage.py` (scans the `first` field of dirfrag omap values and raw `mds_snaptable` bytes); `cephfs-meta-injection` (reads and amends dentry values and fnode headers); and `ceph-dencoder` (decodes fnode_t, inode_t, InodeStore, inode_backtrace_t, InoTable, SnapServer, session_info_t, Anchor, PurgeItem, JournalPointer, Journaler::Header, most events, MMDSTableRequest). Operator procedures in doc/cephfs/disaster-recovery-experts.rst rely on these tools and object names.
features.notes: cephfs-data-scan never sets a RADOS namespace, so `scan_extents` sees no data written under `pool_ns`. An interrupted data-scan run leaves dentries with `first = CEPH_NOSNAP`, which the MDS treats as corrupt until `first-damage.py --repair-nosnap` (rados-object-catalog section 8). Tool overview: [mgr, tools and orchestration](../cpp-map/01-cluster-integration/mgr-tools-and-orchestration.md).

features.group: Observability, offline tools and test knobs
features.name: Developer and fault-injection options
features.summary: Dev-only options that pause, kill or corrupt the journal and table paths for testing.
features.description: `mds_log_pause` (the submit thread stops dequeuing until cleared), `mds_kill_journal_expire_at` 1-5, `mds_kill_journal_replay_at` 1-4, `mds_kill_mdstable_at` 1-9 (server prepare, prepare logged, client agree, client commit, server commit, commit logged, client ack, server rollback, client notify-prep), `mds_inject_skip_replaying_inotable`, `mds_inject_journal_corrupt_dentry_first`, `mds_delay_journal_replay_for_testing`, `mds_debug_subtrees` (journals an `EVENT_SUBTREEMAP_TEST` (50) whenever the segment has more than one event), `mds_debug_frag`, `mds_standby_replay_damaged`. `mds_kill_journal_at` exists but nothing reads it.
features.notes: `EVENT_SUBTREEMAP_TEST` events are still `SegmentBoundary` objects, so with `mds_debug_subtrees` every second event starts a new major segment, contrary to the code comment (mdlog-and-journaler section 8 item 3). These options are used by the QA suites. See also F-ADM-065.
